definition_zh: 蝎子；蝎座；阴险的人
definition_en: a small animal with eight legs and a curved tail that can sting
core_image: 沙地上高举弯曲尾巴的甲壳小动物，两只钳子张开
scene: 沙漠夜里，石缝中探出一截弯曲的尾巴，尖端闪了一下。A scorpion walked slowly across the warm sand and raised its tail.
sceneCN: 这里 scorpion 是「蝎子」（第 1 个义项：有八条腿、尾巴带刺节肢动物）；句意：一只蝎子慢慢爬过温热的沙地，翘起了尾巴。

collocations.zh: 石头下的蝎子（暗藏的危险）

derivatives.zh: 由 scorpion 与 fish 合成，指「鲉」，因背鳍带毒刺形似蝎尾
由 scorpion 与 fly 合成，指「蝎蛉」，雄虫腹部末端上弯如蝎尾
拉丁语词形，英语中作天蝎座名称
义为「蝎尾状的」，植物学中形容花序卷曲如蝎尾

senses.title: An eight-legged animal with a stinging tail
senses.definition: a small predatory animal with eight legs, pincers and a curved tail ending in a sting
senses.definitionCN: 一种小型捕食动物，有八条腿、钳子，以及末端带毒刺的弯曲尾巴
senses.example: The scorpion hid beneath a flat rock until morning.
senses.exampleCN: 那只蝎子躲在一块扁石下，一直待到早晨。
senses.why: The Latin name came from Greek words for its pincers and its curved tail, so the creature is named for the very shape we still picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名源自希腊语中表示钳子与弯曲尾巴的词，因此这种动物正是按我们脑海里的形状命名的。

senses.title: The zodiac sign and constellation
senses.definition: the eighth sign of the zodiac, shown as a scorpion
senses.definitionCN: 黄道第八宫，形象为蝎子
senses.example: The night sky shows the stars of the scorpion clearly in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天的夜空清楚地现出天蝎座的群星。
senses.why: Ancient sky-watchers saw the animal in a line of stars, so the creature name became a picture in the heavens.
senses.whyCN: 古代观星者在一串星星中看出一只蝎子，于是这种动物的名字成了天上的图案。

senses.title: A person who hides a sting
senses.definition: a figure of speech for someone cruel or dangerous who attacks from hiding
senses.definitionCN: 比喻阴险危险、躲在暗处伤人的恶人
senses.example: The old proverb warns that a smooth tongue may hide a scorpion.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的谚语告诫人们，甜言蜜语也许藏着一条蝎尾。
senses.why: A scorpion waits quietly and stings without warning, so the animal becomes shorthand for a hidden, scheming person.
senses.whyCN: 蝎子静静蛰伏、出其不意地蜇人，因此这种动物成了暗中算计之人的代名词。

intro.en: Scorpion comes from Latin scorpio, which is related to Greek skorpios; the Greek word was also applied to a stinging fish and to a war engine, and its ultimate origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: scorpion 来自拉丁语 scorpio，与希腊语 skorpios 相关；希腊语这个词也用来指一种会蜇人的鱼和一种攻城器械，其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Skorpios names the animal and, by extension, a stinging fish and a siege engine.
items.cn: skorpios 指这种动物，并引申指会蜇的鱼和攻城器械。

items.en: Scorpio carries the animal name; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: scorpio 承载这一动物名称；更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Historians and writers record the creature name as escorpion.
items.cn: 史家与作家以 escorpion 记录这种动物之名。

items.en: The noun enters English with the spelling scorpion.
items.cn: 这个词以 scorpion 的拼写进入中古英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the animal, adds the zodiac sign, and adds the figure of a cruel person.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动物义，又加上星座义与「恶人」的比喻义。

note.en: Scorpion belongs to the world of arachnids, neighbours of spider and tick, and its spelling siblings include scorpionfish and scorpionfly.
note.cn: scorpion 属于蛛形动物一类，与 spider、tick 为邻；形近词还有 scorpionfish 与 scorpionfly。

entries.definition: a spiny fish with venomous spines that hurts like a sting
entries.definitionCN: 带毒刺的鲉，被刺后疼痛如蝎蜇

entries.definition: an insect whose male has a tail curled like a stinger
entries.definitionCN: 一种昆虫，雄虫尾部卷曲如蝎尾

entries.definition: Latin form, used in English for the zodiac sign
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语词形，英语中作天蝎座名称

entries.definition: an eight-legged animal that spins webs
entries.definitionCN: 八条腿、会结网的蜘蛛

entries.definition: a small eight-legged creature that sucks blood
entries.definitionCN: 吸血的八腿小虫

entries.definition: a sharp wound made by a plant or animal
entries.definitionCN: 植物或动物的蜇刺

normalIntro.en: Scorpion is a borrowed animal name, carried through Latin and Greek, with two kinds of hook to remember: the pincers and the tail.
normalIntro.cn: scorpion 是借来的动物名，经拉丁语与希腊语传入英语，可用两样钩子来记：钳子与尾巴。

normal.en: The Latin name is scorpio, the same word used for the zodiac sign.
normal.cn: 拉丁名 scorpio 同时也是天蝎座的名称。

normal.en: A scorpion sting means a sharp and sudden hurt.
normal.cn: a scorpion sting 表示尖锐而突然的伤害。

normal.en: Scorpion and spider are both arachnids, but scorpions have a tail.
normal.cn: 蝎子与蜘蛛同属蛛形动物，但蝎子有尾巴。

normal.en: Scorpionfish and scorpionfly are named for their scorpion-like spines and tails.
normal.cn: 鲉与蝎蛉因毒刺和卷尾形似蝎子而得名。

normal.en: The scorpion in a proverb stands for a hidden, cunning enemy.
normal.cn: 谚语中的蝎子象征暗藏的狡猾敌人。

abstract.en: Picture two open pincers and one high tail on a patch of warm sand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只张开双钳、高举尾巴的家伙停在温热的沙地上。

abstract.en: Picture a line of stars curling like a tail across the summer night.
abstract.cn: 想象夏夜的星带弯成一条尾巴。

abstract.en: Picture a smooth voice in a crowded room while something cold hides under the table.
abstract.cn: 想象热闹房间里一句温柔的嗓音，而桌下藏着冰冷的危险。

examples.en: The scorpion disappeared into the crack before the torch light reached it.
examples.cn: 手电的光还没照到，蝎子已钻进了石缝。

examples.en: Scorpions and spiders share eight legs, so both belong to the arachnids.
examples.cn: 蝎子和蜘蛛都有八条腿，因此都属于蛛形动物。

examples.en: Her letter called him a scorpion dressed in fine clothes.
examples.cn: 她在信里说他是披着华服的蝎子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯科皮昂」——读音像一位昂着头、翘着皮的怪客；记住皮字下的扁身，就是蝎子的样子；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 skorpios（蝎子，也指会蜇的鱼与攻城器械）→ 拉丁语 scorpio（蝎子；天蝎座）→ 古法语 escorpion → 中古英语 scorpion → 英语 scorpion，更深词源不确定，核心义「举尾带刺的小型节肢动物」。

sensesIntro.en: Scorpion names the stinging animal, then the star shape that recalls it, and finally a person who stings in secret.
sensesIntro.cn: scorpion 先指举尾带刺的动物，再指形似它的星象，最后指暗中蜇人的恶人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small armoured creature with open pincers and a raised stinging tail.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只披甲的小动物，张着钳子、翘着带刺的尾巴。

branches.en: The living animal is the literal, basic sense.
branches.cn: 活的动物是字面的基本义项。

branches.en: The zodiac sign borrows the animal shape for the sky.
branches.cn: 星座义把动物的形状借到了天上。

branches.en: A hidden stinger becomes a figure for a cruel person.
branches.cn: 暗中蜇人者成了形容恶人的比喻。

branches.en: Both the animal and the constellation share the curled tail.
branches.cn: 动物与星座共享那条弯成钩的尾巴。

branches.en: The waiting sting of the animal gives the human insult its force.
branches.cn: 动物蓄势待发的刺，给了骂人的说法以力量。

intro.en: Scorpion is not built from productive English pieces; its compounds scorpionfish and scorpionfly merely attach ordinary nouns to the borrowed name.
intro.cn: scorpion 不是用能产的英语词缀构成的；它的复合词 scorpionfish 与 scorpionfly 只是在借来的名称后接普通名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin scorpio, related to Greek skorpios, names the animal and the zodiac sign, and Latin also lends scorpio its figurative use.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scorpio 与希腊语 skorpios 相关，兼指该动物与星座，其比喻用法也源于拉丁传统。

items.example: Scorpion keeps the borrowed name unchanged.
items.exampleCN: scorpion 保留借来的原样名称。

items.example: The suffix -s gives scorpions.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 scorpions。

items.example: Scorpions are common in dry regions.
items.exampleCN: scorpions 在干旱地区很常见。

items.example: Fish joins scorpion to name a spiny sea fish.
items.exampleCN: fish 与 scorpion 合成带刺海鱼的名字。

items.example: Scorpionfish stings are painful.
items.exampleCN: 鲉的蜇伤很疼。

items.example: Fly joins scorpion to name a tailed insect.
items.exampleCN: fly 与 scorpion 合成一种卷尾昆虫的名称。

items.meaning: an insect with a scorpion-like tail
items.example: A scorpionfly cannot sting.
items.exampleCN: 蝎蛉并不会蜇人。

items.example: The suffix -oid gives scorpioid.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -oid 构成 scorpioid。

items.example: A scorpioid flower cluster curls like a tail.
items.exampleCN: 蝎尾状花序卷曲如尾巴。

latinEntries.meaning: a scorpion, later a stinging war engine
latinEntries.meaningCN: 蝎子；后指会蜇刺的攻城器械

latinEntries.meaning: an older variant used for the constellation
latinEntries.meaningCN: 较古的变体，用于星座名

definition_zh: 擦洗；冲刷；彻底搜寻；扫荡；侵蚀
definition_en: to clean a surface by hard rubbing, to search a place very carefully, or for water to cut away material and leave bare rock
core_image: 一只手拿粗布或钢刷在锅底来回猛擦，把污垢刮掉
scene: 老式厨房里水汽弥漫，一口焦黑的铁锅泡在水池中。She spent twenty minutes scouring the burnt pan with a steel brush.
sceneCN: 这里 scour 是「用力擦洗」（第 1 个义项：用硬刷等把表面擦得干净发亮）；句意为她用钢丝刷花了二十分钟猛擦那口烧焦的锅。画面可辨识物件：水槽、铁锅、钢刷、水汽。

pos.zh: 擦洗；冲刷（一处被冲成的洼地）

collocations.zh: 搜遍乡野；在乡间四处搜索

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「擦洗的人；钢丝刷、百洁布」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「擦洗；冲刷」或「擦洗用的」
由过去分词形容词化，义为「被冲刷过的；擦得发亮的」

senses.title: To rub a surface hard until it is clean
senses.definition: to clean something by rubbing it very hard with a rough cloth, brush or cleaning powder
senses.definitionCN: 用粗布、刷子或去污粉等使劲摩擦，使表面洁净
senses.example: She scoured the sink until the stains disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 她把水槽擦洗到污渍完全消失。
senses.why: The oldest English sense is literally to scrub hard, and it gave the word its picture of a hand rubbing back and forth until the surface is bare.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项，本义就是使劲擦，核心画面是手来回摩擦，直到表面露出本色。

senses.title: To remove dirt or marks by hard rubbing
senses.definition: to get rid of dirt, rust, grease or marks by rubbing them away
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复摩擦除去污垢、锈迹、油渍或痕迹
senses.example: He scoured the rust off the old spade with sandpaper.
senses.exampleCN: 他用砂纸把旧铁锹上的锈磨掉了。
senses.why: When the rubbing is aimed at a particular mark, the verb shifts from cleaning the thing to removing the substance.
senses.whyCN: 当摩擦针对某一处具体的痕迹时，动词的宾语就从「物件」转到「被磨掉的物质」，于是长出「擦掉」这一义。

senses.title: To search a place very thoroughly
senses.definition: to search a place or group very carefully and completely, usually for something specific
senses.definitionCN: 为寻找某物而极其仔细、彻底地搜索某地或某群体
senses.example: Police scoured the woods for the missing child.
senses.exampleCN: 警方为寻找失踪的孩子搜遍了那片树林。
senses.why: Searching a place exactly as one scours a pan leaves no spot untouched, so the cleaning image became a metaphor of exhaustive search.
senses.whyCN: 搜遍一个地方，就像把锅的每个角落都擦到一样不留死角；擦洗所隐含的「无一处遗漏」变成了彻底搜寻的比喻。

senses.title: To move quickly and forcefully over an area
senses.definition: to move rapidly across an area, especially in order to look for, chase or attack someone
senses.definitionCN: 迅速而强力地掠过或穿过某区域，尤指为了寻找、追击或攻击某人
senses.example: The storm scoured the coastline before moving inland.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴扫过海岸线后才向内陆移动。
senses.why: A rapid sweep repeats the sideways motion of the scrubbing cloth, now over ground instead of a surface.
senses.whyCN: 快速扫过延续了擦布横向抹过的动作，只是摩擦的对象从器皿表面换成了地面。

senses.title: For water to wear away ground and rock
senses.definition: for moving water, wind or ice to wear away soil and rock, often leaving a channel behind
senses.definitionCN: 流动的水、风或冰磨蚀土层和岩层，往往留下沟槽
senses.example: The flood scoured a deep channel through the field.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水在田里冲出很深的一道沟。
senses.why: A river rubbing its bed is nature doing what a brush does to a pan, so the earth and rock are literally scoured away.
senses.whyCN: 河床被水流反复摩擦，就是大自然在做刷子擦锅的事，土石因此被实实在在地「擦」掉。

senses.title: Bare, worn and empty after being stripped
senses.definition: describing a surface or place that has been stripped bare by fast water, wind or ice
senses.definitionCN: 形容表面或地方被急流、风或冰剥蚀得毫无遮盖
senses.example: Only a thin layer of soil survives on the scoured bedrock.
senses.exampleCN: 被冲刷过的岩床上只剩薄薄一层土。
senses.why: Once erosion has carried everything loose away, what remains is a clean surface, and clean in its harshest form means bare.
senses.whyCN: 侵蚀把所有松散的东西都带走后，剩下的是一块「干净」的表面，而最极端的干净就是光秃。

senses.title: A rapid sweep in search of something
senses.definition: a quick but thorough search or sweep of an area by a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 一群人对某区域进行快速而彻底的搜索或扫荡
senses.example: A final scour of the beach found no trace of the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一次搜遍海滩也没有找到那只船的踪迹。
senses.why: English turns many verb actions into countable nouns, so the act of scouring becomes a scour, a single complete sweep.
senses.whyCN: 英语里动作动词常可转成可数名词，擦扫一遍的动作就被记成一次 scour，即一整趟扫荡式搜索。

senses.title: Slimmer through illness or stress
senses.titleCN: （因疾病或压力）消瘦，形容枯槁
senses.definition: to make a person or animal very thin and worn, as if the flesh has been scraped away
senses.definitionCN: 使人或动物变得极度消瘦、憔悴，仿佛皮肉被刮掉一般
senses.example: Fever had scoured the boy until his cheekbones stood out.
senses.exampleCN: 高烧折磨得男孩日渐消瘦，颧骨都突了出来。
senses.why: The older English sense of scouring as a violent passing of illness carries the cleaning image into the body, where what is rubbed away is flesh.
senses.whyCN: 古英语时期 scour 也指疫病迅疾肆虐，擦洗的意象被带进身体，被抹掉的成了血肉，于是有了「消瘦」的引申义。

intro.en: Scour probably comes from Old Norse skura, to clean or scrub, which was brought in by Scandinavian settlers and then reshaped under the influence of Latin excurare.
intro.cn: scour 一般认为来自古诺斯语 skura（清洗、刷洗），由斯堪的纳维亚移民带入英语，后来在拉丁语 excurare（仔细清除）的影响下改变了词形。

items.en: Skura means to scrub or clean, and skur means a shower or storm; the cleaning and the rushing meanings sit side by side.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 skura 意为刷洗、清洗，同源名词 skur 意为阵雨、风暴；「洗净」和「疾冲」两种含义并存在词根里。

items.en: The word enters Middle English as scouren, used for scrubbing clothes and dishes and for the swift passage of sickness.
items.cn: scour 以 scouren 进入中古英语，既用于搓洗衣物、刷洗餐具，也指疫病迅疾而过。

items.en: Some forms come close to Latin excurare, with ex- and curare, to care for, so careful cleaning reinforced the native word.
items.cn: 部分词形接近拉丁语 excurare（由 ex- 与 curare「照料」构成），「仔细清洗」的观念反过来强化了这个本族词。

items.en: The verb extends from pots to rivers, as moving water scours a bed, and to soldiers scouring a district in search of something.
items.cn: 16 至 17 世纪，动词的对象从锅具扩展到河道（水流冲刷河床），也扩展到军队扫荡某一地区以搜寻目标。

items.en: Geologists adopt the word for ice and flood water that wear bedrock bare, giving the sense of a scoured landscape.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学家用它描写冰与洪水把基岩磨得光秃，于是有了「被冲刷过的地貌」这一用法。

items.en: The verb now also covers searching online or a room, and the noun names a sweep of search.
items.cn: 现代英语中它还可以指在网上或房间里四处翻找，名词则指一次扫荡式的搜索。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the sc- scraping cluster and the same speed-and-cleanance imagery; the near-meaning group separates scrubbing from rinsing and thorough searching from a quick look.
note.cn: 形近组收 sc- 开头、同样带「刮擦」意味的一族词；近义组区别「擦洗」与「冲洗」，以及「彻底搜寻」与「快速查看」。

entries.definition: A person or a rough pad used for scouring pots and pans.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「擦洗者；钢丝刷、百洁布」，由本词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Cleaned by hard rubbing, or worn bare by fast water; formed from the past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，义为「擦净的；被急流冲刷得光秃的」，由过去分词形容词化而成。

entries.definition: The process of scrubbing or of being worn away by fast water; also used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「擦洗；冲刷」，也可作定语，如冲刷造成的沟槽；别与形近的 scowl（怒视、皱眉）混淆，后者词源无关。

entries.definition: To rub something hard with a brush and water; closest to scour, but often part of a wash rather than the final shine.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「刷洗」，与 scour 最近，但多是一整套洗涤中的一步，不如 scour 强调擦到发亮。

entries.definition: To wash lightly with clean water, removing soap rather than dirt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「冲洗、冲洗掉」，用水轻洗，冲走的是泡沫而非污垢，力度比 scour 小得多。

entries.definition: To search a place very carefully; a strong synonym for the search sense of scour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「仔细搜寻」，是 scour「彻底搜寻」义的强近义词，形象是用梳子一遍遍梳理。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real history of the word: Norse scrubbing, then water wearing rock, then people sweeping a district.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子沿着这个词的真实历史走：先是北欧话里的刷洗，再是被水磨蚀，最后是人扫荡一片区域。

normal.en: The cleaning sense is the oldest: to scour is to scrub until the surface is bare.
normal.cn: 清洗义最古老：scour 就是一直刷，刷到露出本色。

normal.en: The search sense copies the cleaning: leave no corner unscrubbed, leave no corner unsearched.
normal.cn: 搜寻义是清洗义的延长：没有角落不被刷过，也就没有角落没被搜过。

normal.en: The erosion sense is the planet doing the scrubbing: fast water rubs a river bed and carves a channel.
normal.cn: 侵蚀义是地球自己在刷洗：急流摩擦河床，冲出一条沟。

normal.en: Remember the pair scour and scrubbing: same hard rubbing, different vowel.
normal.cn: 记住 scour 与 scrubbing 这一对：都是拼命摩擦，只是元音不同。

normal.en: In news English, police are said to scour an area for a suspect.
normal.cn: 在新闻英语里，常说警方为寻找嫌疑人而 scour 某片区域。

abstract.en: Picture a steel brush moving in circles on a burnt pan until the metal shines.
abstract.cn: 想象钢刷在烧焦的锅底一圈圈打转，直到金属闪出光。

abstract.en: Picture a flashlight beam sweeping the same pan, now a whole dark room that must be searched.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条光束扫过那只锅，现在扫的是一整间必须搜遍的暗房。

abstract.en: Picture a river as the brush and the stone as the pan, worn smooth after thousands of years.
abstract.cn: 想象河流是那把刷子、石头是那只锅，被磨去棱角几千年。

examples.en: Volunteers scoured the beach for the missing wallet.
examples.cn: 志愿者们把海滩搜了个遍，寻找丢失的钱包。

examples.en: The river has scoured a narrow gorge through the limestone.
examples.cn: 河水在石灰岩中冲出一条狭窄的峡谷。

examples.en: Use hot water and a stiff brush to scour the burnt pot.
examples.cn: 用热水和硬毛刷把烧焦的锅使劲刷干净。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死抠」——锅底焦糊要死抠着刷才干净；搜东西时也是死抠每个角落。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自古诺斯语 skura「刷洗、清洗」，同族名词 skur 意为「阵雨、风暴」，因此「猛刷」与「疾冲」两种意象始终并存；中古英语拼作 scouren，词形又受拉丁语 excurare「仔细清除」影响。印欧语层面的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Scour starts with a hand rubbing a surface clean, then extends to removing what was rubbed away, to sweeping a whole area in search of something, and to water wearing away rock.
sensesIntro.cn: scour 从「用手把表面擦干净」出发，延伸到「把擦下来的东西除掉」，再到「扫遍整片区域去找」，最后落到水流磨蚀岩层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand rubs a steel brush across a burnt pan until the surface gleams.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把钢刷压在焦锅上来回猛擦，直到表面发亮。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN: scrubbing a surface clean and rubbing dirt or rust off it are the two halves of a single gesture.
branches.cn: 厨房线：把表面刷净与把污垢锈迹磨掉，是同一个动作的两面。

branches.en: THE SEARCH: covering an area without a gap becomes a thorough hunt, and one full sweep becomes a scour.
branches.cn: 搜寻线：把一片区域毫无遗漏地走遍，成为彻底搜寻；走完一趟，就是一次 scour。

branches.en: THE LAND: fast water rubs a river bed and strips the ground until only bare rock is left.
branches.cn: 土地线：急流摩擦河床、剥去地表，最后只剩光秃的岩石。

branches.en: THE FAST PASS: the sideways motion of the cloth becomes a storm or a patrol sweeping across it.
branches.cn: 掠扫线：擦布横向抹过的动作，变成风暴或巡逻队迅疾扫过地面。

branches.en: THE BODY: an old medical use treats fever as a force that scrubs the flesh away.
branches.cn: 身体线：旧时医学用法把高烧看作把血肉刮走的力量。

intro.en: Scour is a short Germanic verb with no Latin prefix or suffix, so the family grows by adding ordinary English endings such as -er, -ing and -ed.
intro.cn: scour 是一个简短的日耳曼语动词，本身没有拉丁前缀或后缀，词族靠加 -er、-ing、-ed 等普通英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no direct ancestor of scour; the only Latin contact is excurare, which shaped the spelling and may have added the idea of careful cleaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语并非 scour 的直接来源，唯一的接触是 excurare，它影响了拼写，可能也带来了「仔细清洗」的观念。

items.example: Skura is the likely ancestor of scour.
items.exampleCN: skura 是 scour 可能的祖先。

items.example: Skur adds the idea of rushing water.
items.exampleCN: skur 带来「疾水冲过」的意象。

items.meaning: to clean out thoroughly, to care for
items.example: Excurare pushed the English spelling towards scoure.
items.exampleCN: excurare 把英语拼写推向 scoure。

items.example: Scouren is the Middle English form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: scouren 是这个动词的中古英语形式。

items.meaning: person or tool that does something
items.example: The suffix -er forms scourer from scour plus a rough pad.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 scourer，指擦洗者或擦洗用的粗糙垫子。

items.meaning: a person who scours, or a pad for scrubbing
items.example: Scourer is the everyday tool noun for the kitchen.
items.exampleCN: scourer 是厨房里常见的工具名词。

items.meaning: the act or process of doing something
items.example: The suffix -ing forms the noun scouring.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成名词 scouring。

items.meaning: hard rubbing, or the wearing away of a river bed
items.example: Scouring also names the erosion that carves a channel.
items.exampleCN: scouring 也可指冲出沟槽的侵蚀作用。

items.meaning: past tense, or having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ed makes the adjective scoured.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成形容词 scoured。

items.meaning: cleaned by rubbing, or worn bare by water
items.meaningCN: 擦净的；被冲刷得光秃的
items.example: Scoured rock shows where flood water once ran.
items.exampleCN: 光秃的岩石显示洪水曾在哪里流过。

latinEntries.meaning: to clean out, to remove carefully

definition_zh: 碎片；废料；剩饭；争吵；小规模冲突；废弃；取消
definition_en: a small piece left over or torn off, waste material such as old metal, a short fight, or the act of throwing something away
core_image: 一块从整张纸上撕下来的不规则小片，被丢在桌角
scene: 车间地板上堆着拆下来的旧铁片，一名工人正在把它们装进推车。Every month the factory sells its old machines for scrap.
sceneCN: 这里 scrap 是「废料；废金属」（第 3 个义项：可回收利用的废弃物）；句意为这家工厂每月都把旧机器当废铁卖掉。画面可辨识物件：推车、旧铁片、扳手、铁屑。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「零散的；拼凑的；好斗的」
由本词与 book 复合，义为「剪贴簿」
由「打架」义加 -er 构成，义为「爱打架的人；斗士」
由本词与 heap 复合，义为「废料堆」，常用于把某人称作过时无用

senses.title: A small piece torn or left over
senses.definition: a small piece of something, especially one that has been torn, cut off or left over
senses.definitionCN: 某物的一小块，尤指撕下、切下或剩下的一小片
senses.example: He wrote the number on a scrap of paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他把号码写在一小片纸上。
senses.why: Old Norse skrap meant odds and ends, and the English noun kept that sense of a loose fragment detached from a whole.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 skrap 指零碎的东西，英语名词保留了「从整体上脱落下来的松散碎块」这一意象。

senses.title: Leftover food with little value
senses.definition: small amounts of food left after a meal, or unwanted bits of food that are thrown out
senses.definitionCN: 饭后剩下的一点食物，或不想要的、可丢弃的零碎食物
senses.example: They fed the vegetable scraps to the chickens.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把剩菜碎叶喂给鸡吃。
senses.why: Food bits are the fragments of a meal, so the small-piece sense naturally names what is left on plates and chopping boards.
senses.whyCN: 食物碎屑就是一餐饭的「碎片」，所以「小块」义顺理成章指向盘中、案板上剩下的东西。

senses.title: Waste material that can be reused
senses.definition: unwanted material such as old metal, machinery or paper that is still worth selling or melting down
senses.definitionCN: 旧金属、旧机器、废纸等不再需要却仍可出售或熔炼的材料
senses.example: The old ship was sold for scrap.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘旧船被当废铁卖掉了。
senses.why: Once a broken object is pulled apart it is all fragments, and those fragments are exactly what the scrapyard buys by weight.
senses.whyCN: 报废的物件一旦拆开就全是碎片，而废品回收站正是按重量收购这些碎片，于是「碎片」变成了「废料」。

senses.title: A short angry quarrel or fight
senses.definition: a brief, often noisy quarrel or fight, usually between two people or two small groups
senses.definitionCN: 简短而通常嘈杂的争吵或打斗，多见于两人或两小群之间
senses.example: The brothers had a scrap about who should wash up.
senses.exampleCN: 兄弟俩为谁来洗碗吵了一架。
senses.why: A fight can be pictured as things being torn into pieces, and the noun for torn-off pieces also names a short, broken-up struggle.
senses.whyCN: 打架可以想象成把东西撕成碎片，于是「撕下的碎块」这一名词也用来指一场短促的、碎片式的打斗。

senses.title: To throw something away as useless
senses.definition: to get rid of something, especially equipment, a vehicle or a plan, because it is old, damaged or no longer useful
senses.definitionCN: 因为老旧、损坏或不再有用而弃置某物，尤指设备、车辆或计划
senses.example: The company scrapped its old delivery vans.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把旧的送货车报废了。
senses.why: If the noun names pieces thrown on the scrap heap, the verb is the act of putting something there, so to scrap is to reduce it to a piece of waste.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词指堆在废料场上的碎片，动词就是把东西送进那里的动作，scrap 因此等于把某物降为一件废料。

senses.title: To cancel a plan or project
senses.definition: to decide not to continue with a plan, project, policy or system
senses.definitionCN: 决定不再继续某项计划、工程、政策或制度
senses.example: The council scrapped the bus route after low demand.
senses.exampleCN: 因为需求不足，市政会取消这条公交线路。
senses.why: Reaching the same end another way, a cancelled plan is simply tossed onto the pile of things not worth keeping.
senses.whyCN: 换一条路走到同样的终点：被取消的计划不过是被扔进「不值得留」那一堆里的东西。

senses.title: A small amount that barely exists
senses.titleCN: 一丁点；丝毫（多用于否定）
senses.definition: a very small amount of something abstract, such as evidence, comfort or trust
senses.definitionCN: 抽象事物（如证据、安慰、信任）的极小数量
senses.example: There is not a scrap of evidence to support the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 没有任何一点证据支持这一说法。
senses.why: The fragment sense counts abstract things too, but only in negative or tiny amounts, because a scrap is barely anything at all.
senses.whyCN: 碎片义也能用来数抽象事物，但只出现在否定或极微量的语境里，因为碎片本身就等于「几乎没有」。

senses.title: A small picture or news cutting
senses.titleCN: （报刊上的）小图片、短新闻剪报
senses.definition: a short piece of news or a small picture cut out of a newspaper or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 从报纸杂志上剪下来的一小段新闻或小图片
senses.example: She kept a scrap from the newspaper about the discovery.
senses.exampleCN: 她保存了一份关于那次发现的报纸剪报。
senses.why: A cutting is literally a small piece taken from a larger printed whole, so the word covers clippings as well.
senses.whyCN: 剪报就是从整份报纸上取下的一小块，所以这个词也覆盖剪下来的新闻与图片。

intro.en: Scrap was probably borrowed from Old Norse skrap, odds and ends, which is linked to the verb skrapa, to scratch; older dictionaries sometimes explain it another way, so the exact route is uncertain.
intro.cn: scrap 一般认为借自古诺斯语 skrap「零碎杂物」，与动词 skrapa「刮、擦」相关；早期词典曾给出另一种解释，确切来源不确定。

items.en: Skrap means odds and ends or rubbish, and the related verb skrapa means to scratch or scrape something off.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 skrap 意为零碎杂物、垃圾，相关动词 skrapa 意为刮擦、刮掉。

items.en: Scrap appears in English as a small piece or a bit of something, recorded from the late fourteenth century onward.
items.cn: scrap 最早出现在英语中，指一小块、一点东西，自十四世纪后期起有记录。

items.en: Industrial writing uses scrap for old metal and broken machinery that is sold or melted down.
items.cn: 十八世纪的工业文献开始用 scrap 指可出售或回炉的旧金属与破损机器。

items.en: The verb to scrap, to throw away as waste, grows out of the noun, along with scrapbook and scrapyard.
items.cn: 动词「废弃」义由名词长出，与之同期的还有 scrapbook（剪贴簿）与 scrapyard（废品场）。

items.en: Colloquial sport writing gives scrap the sense of a short fight, and later of a brief quarrel.
items.cn: 口语化的体育报道让 scrap 获得「短促打架」义，后来又引申出简短争吵。

items.en: Business and politics use the verb for cancelling a plan, so a scrapped project joins the scrap heap of discarded ideas.
items.cn: 现代商务与政治话语用这个动词表示取消计划，被取消的项目就被扔进淘汰想法的废料堆。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same scratching and fragment root; the near-meaning group separates a torn fragment from a fragment left after use, and a short fight from a formal one.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「刮擦、碎片」词根下的一族词；近义组区分「撕裂的碎片」与「用剩的碎屑」，以及「短促打架」与「正式战斗」。

entries.definition: To drag something hard across a surface, often to remove a layer or to scratch it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「刮、刮掉」，与 scrap 同出一系，强调贴着表面拖动。

entries.definition: A tool with a flat edge used to scrape paint or ice off a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「刮刀、铲子」，用来刮去表面上的漆或冰；来自 scrape 加 -er，与 scrap 相连但属另一条派生线。

entries.definition: Made of scattered bits or of small disconnected parts, or determined and fond of fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「零散的、拼凑的」或「不认输、好斗的」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: A part of something, neutral in tone and size; a scrap is smaller, odd and usually left over.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一块、一部分」，语气中性，大小不限；scrap 更小、更零散，多是剩下的。

entries.definition: A part broken off from something larger; more formal and more often used of speech or stone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「碎片」，多指从较大物体上断裂下来的部分，语气比 scrap 正式。

entries.definition: Things that are no longer wanted and are thrown away; British and broader than scrap, which can still be sold.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾」，英式英语常用，范围比 scrap 宽；scrap 通常还能回收出售，另有「争吵、扭打」义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the word from a scratched-off bit to a fight and finally to a cancelled plan.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子沿着这个词的轨迹走：从刮下来的碎块，到一场短打，最后到被取消的计划。

normal.en: Scrape a pan and you get scraps: the same scratch gives both the verb and the bit.
normal.cn: 刮一刮锅就刮下碎屑：同一个刮的动作，既生出动词 scrape，也生出碎块 scrap。

normal.en: A scrap of paper is the smallest thing you can still write on.
normal.cn: a scrap of paper 就是还能写上字的最小的一张纸。

normal.en: A scrap heap is where machines go after their last day of work.
normal.cn: scrap heap 就是机器干完最后一天之后去的地方。

normal.en: In sport, a scrap is a short fight; a scrap of a match is close and rough.
normal.cn: 在体育里，scrap 指短促的打架；一场 scrappy 的比赛就是又接近又粗野。

normal.en: To scrap a plan is to treat the plan as a piece of waste paper.
normal.cn: to scrap a plan 就是把计划当成一张废纸扔掉。

abstract.en: Picture a single torn corner of a page lying on the floor beside a neat stack of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被撕下的一角落在整整齐齐一摞纸旁边的地板上。

abstract.en: Picture the same corner on a dinner plate after the meal, now a leftover bit of carrot.
abstract.cn: 想象它出现在饭后的盘子里，变成了一小块剩胡萝卜。

abstract.en: Picture a mountain of these bits by a shipyard gate, weighed and sold by the tonne.
abstract.cn: 想象船厂门口堆起一座碎块小山，按吨称重后卖掉。

examples.en: Bring a pen and a scrap of paper to the interview.
examples.cn: 面试时带上一支笔和一小片纸。

examples.en: The council scrapped plans for a new car park.
examples.cn: 市政会取消了修建新停车场的计划。

examples.en: Neighbours had a scrap over the noise from the party.
examples.cn: 邻居们因为聚会的噪音吵了一架。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撕刮破」——纸被撕开、一刮就破，掉下来的就是碎片、废料。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为借自古诺斯语 skrap「零碎杂物、垃圾」，与动词 skrapa「刮、擦」同根；英语早期词典另有一种解释，确切来源不确定。核心义始终是「从整体上被刮下、撕下的一小块」。

sensesIntro.en: Scrap begins as a small piece off a larger thing, spreads to leftover food and waste metal, and then to a torn-up fight, a thrown-away plan and finally a tiny amount of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: scrap 从「从整体上取下的一小块」出发，扩散到剩饭与废金属，再长出「撕扯式的小打斗」「被扔掉的计划」，最后表示任何东西的极小数量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a torn, irregular piece of paper is left on the corner of a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块撕下来的不规则纸片被丢在桌角。

branches.en: THE PARTICLE: paper, food and newspaper cuttings are all fragments of a larger whole.
branches.cn: 碎块线：纸片、食物碎屑、剪报都是从更大整体上取下的一小块。

branches.en: THE YARD: broken machines become saleable fragments, and turning an object into one is what the verb means.
branches.cn: 废品场线：坏掉的机器变成可卖的碎块，而动词所指正是把物件变成这种碎块。

branches.en: THE DRAWER: a cancelled plan is treated exactly like waste paper.
branches.cn: 抽屉线：被取消的计划，待遇与废纸完全相同。

branches.en: THE STREET: a quarrel or fight is a short struggle that breaks things apart briefly.
branches.cn: 街巷线：争吵或打架就是一场短暂、把东西撕扯开的扭打。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: in negation the tiny fragment measures how little of something abstract exists.
branches.cn: 度量线：在否定句里，这点碎片用来衡量抽象事物少到什么程度。

intro.en: Scrap is a short Germanic noun with a Norse background; English builds its family with -y, -er and the compounds scrapbook and scrapheap.
intro.cn: scrap 是带北欧来源的简短日耳曼语名词，英语靠 -y、-er 以及 scrapbook、scrapheap 等复合方式扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin is not the source of scrap; the word came by way of Old Norse, so no Latin root is claimed here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语并非 scrap 的来源，这个词经由古诺斯语进入英语，因此这里不主张任何拉丁词根。

items.example: Skrap is the probable source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: skrap 是英语名词可能的来源。

items.example: Skrapa explains why scrap and scrape look like twins.
items.exampleCN: skrapa 解释了 scrap 与 scrape 为何像一对双胞胎。

items.example: The suffix -y forms the adjective scrappy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成形容词 scrappy。

items.meaning: made of scattered bits, or determined fighting
items.meaningCN: 零散的、拼凑的；顽强好斗的
items.example: A scrappy notebook is one held together with loose pages.
items.exampleCN: a scrappy notebook 就是由零散纸页拼成的本子。

items.example: The suffix -er forms scrapper from the fight sense.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 从「打架」义构成 scrapper。

items.meaning: a fighter, or a person who sells scrap
items.example: Scrapper is informal and often approving of spirit.
items.exampleCN: scrapper 属口语，常带赞许其斗志的意味。

items.meaning: a book of cuttings and pictures
items.example: A scrapbook keeps small clippings together.
items.exampleCN: scrapbook 把小剪报聚在一起保存。

items.meaning: a yard where old metal is bought and sold
items.example: A scrapyard is where metal scraps are sorted.
items.exampleCN: scrapyard 是分拣废金属的地方。

items.example: To be on the scrapheap is to be cast aside.
items.exampleCN: 「进废料堆」即被弃置一旁、不再需要。

definition_zh: 电影剧本；影片脚本
definition_en: the written text of a film, with dialogue, action and camera directions, used as the plan for shooting it
core_image: 一叠打字稿摊在桌上，左边写动作，右边写台词，中间标着镜头
scene: 深夜的书桌上，台灯照着改了无数遍的稿纸，导演和编剧还在讨论。The screenplay opens with a silent shot of an empty street.
sceneCN: 这里 screenplay 是「电影剧本」（第 1 个义项：用于拍电影、写明动作与台词的文本）；句意为这份剧本以一个空街的无声镜头开场。画面可辨识物件：台灯、稿纸、铅笔、咖啡杯。

collocations.phrase: adapt a novel into a screenplay
collocations.zh: 把小说改编成电影剧本

derivatives.zh: 由 screenplay 与 writer 复合、以「写剧本的人」为义构成，义为「电影编剧」
由 screenwriter 加 -ing 构成，义为「电影编剧工作；剧本创作」
本词的复合成分，义为「银幕；放映；筛选」，是剧本所服务的那块幕布
本词的第二个成分，义为「剧本；剧本稿」，可用于电影、话剧与广播

senses.title: The written text used to make a film
senses.definition: the complete written text of a film, including dialogue, scene headings and descriptions of the action
senses.definitionCN: 一部电影的完整书面文本，包括台词、场次标题与动作描述
senses.example: The studio approved the screenplay last month.
senses.exampleCN: 制片厂上个月通过了这份电影剧本。
senses.why: The word joins screen and play: it is literally a play written for the screen rather than for the stage, and that written plan is what a film is made from.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 screen（银幕）与 play（剧本、戏）拼接而成，本义就是为银幕而非舞台写的戏；这份书面计划正是拍片的依据。

senses.title: The craft or format of writing for films
senses.titleCN: 编剧这一行；电影剧本体裁
senses.definition: the art or professional practice of writing texts for films, or the recognised format such texts follow
senses.definitionCN: 为电影写作文本的艺术或职业，或此类文本所遵循的公认体例
senses.example: She teaches screenplay in the university film department.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学电影系教授电影剧本创作。
senses.why: Named after the thing written, the word also comes to name the trade and the standard layout, since every screenplay follows the same conventions.
senses.whyCN: 以写出的成品命名，这个词也用来指这一行当和标准排版，因为每份电影剧本都遵循同一套体例。

senses.title: An adaptation of another work into film form
senses.titleCN: （由小说等改编成的）改编剧本
senses.definition: a version of a novel, play or true story rewritten in the form used for filming
senses.definitionCN: 把小说、戏剧或真实事件改写成可供拍摄形式的版本
senses.example: His screenplay of the novel keeps only half of its characters.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这部小说改编成的剧本只保留了原著一半的人物。
senses.why: Because the screenplay is the working copy that can be edited, adapted and rewritten, the noun also names each rewrite made from another source.
senses.whyCN: 电影剧本是可以增删改写的工作稿，所以这个名词也指每一次依据其他作品改写的版本。

senses.title: The blueprint that shapes the finished film
senses.definition: the document that guides shooting and editing, so that the finished film is judged against the script
senses.definitionCN: 指导拍摄与剪辑的文本，成片往往被拿来与剧本对照评判
senses.example: In the finished film, the screenplay became a much darker story.
senses.exampleCN: 在最终成片里，这份剧本变成了一个阴暗得多的故事。
senses.why: The written text comes first in time and the picture follows it, so the screenplay works as the blueprint that the whole production is built on.
senses.whyCN: 文字在先、影像在后，整部影片围着这份文本搭建，于是电影剧本成为拍摄的蓝图与骨架。

senses.title: A published version for reading
senses.definition: a screenplay printed and published as a book, often read and studied rather than performed
senses.definitionCN: 以书面形式印制出版的电影剧本，常被阅读和研究，而非演出
senses.example: The screenplay was published with stills from the film.
senses.exampleCN: 这本剧本出版时附带了影片的剧照。
senses.why: A text that guides a film can also stand alone as a reading work, and then the screenplay is sold and studied like a novel.
senses.whyCN: 指导影片的文本也可以独立成篇供人阅读，于是电影剧本像小说一样被出版和研读。

intro.en: Screenplay is an English compound coined in the early twentieth century from screen and play, when the cinema screen took the place of the stage.
intro.cn: screenplay 是二十世纪初由 screen（银幕）与 play（剧本、戏）合成的英语复合词，出现之时电影院银幕正取代舞台。

items.en: The noun screen first means a protective panel or a partition in a room.
items.cn: 名词 screen 最初指防护板或房间里的隔断。

items.en: The screen becomes a device for showing images, and later the surface on which film is projected.
items.cn: screen 逐渐指显示图像的装置，后来又指放映电影的那块幕布。

items.en: The noun play, an acting performance, widens to mean the written text of a drama.
items.cn: 名词 play 原指表演，十九世纪扩展到指戏剧的书面文本。

items.en: Moving pictures need written plans, and the compound screenplay is coined to name a play written for the screen.
items.cn: 电影需要书面计划，于是造出复合词 screenplay，专指为银幕写的戏。

items.en: Screenplay replaces the earlier screen play as one word in professional use, alongside screenwriter and screenwriting.
items.cn: 二十世纪中期，专业用法把原先分写的 screen play 合并成一个词，并出现 screenwriter、screenwriting。

items.en: The word now covers the standard script format, adaptations and published scripts read as literature.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词覆盖标准剧本格式、改编剧本以及被当作文学作品阅读的出版剧本。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on screen or on the script family; the near-meaning group separates writing for the cinema from writing for the stage or for television.
note.cn: 形近组收以 screen 或 script 词族为骨架的词；近义组区分「为电影写」与「为舞台或电视写」。

entries.definition: A person who writes screenplays, usually for a fee.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电影编剧」，与本词共享 screen 词根。

entries.definition: The work or craft of writing screenplays.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电影编剧工作、剧本创作」。

entries.definition: The written text of any dramatic work, used for film, stage, radio or television.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剧本」，可用于电影、舞台、广播或电视，是本词后半部分的单独形式；仅有「银幕；放映」之义的 screen 并不等于剧本。

entries.definition: A written text for stage, radio or film; broader than screenplay and commonly used in everyday talk for the text of a film too.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剧本」，涵盖舞台、广播与电影，范围比 screenplay 宽，日常口语也常用它指电影剧本。

entries.definition: A sequence of drawings that maps out shots; it shows what a screenplay is going to look like.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分镜头草图、故事板」，用一连串图画安排镜头，是电影剧本的视觉化预演。

entries.definition: A prose summary of a film or story, written before the screenplay and much less detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电影故事梗概」，用散文写成，篇幅比重写得早，细节少得多。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two parts of the compound and the film-making words that travel with it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用这个复合词的两个成分，以及总与它一起出现的影视用词。

normal.en: A play on paper is a play; the same play on a screen is a screenplay.
normal.cn: 写在纸上的戏是 play，放到银幕上放映的同一出戏就成了 screenplay。

normal.en: The person is the screenwriter, the job is screenwriting, the text is the screenplay.
normal.cn: 人是 screenwriter，活儿是 screenwriting，文本是 screenplay，三者只差词尾。

normal.en: Write the screenplay first, then draw the storyboard, then shoot.
normal.cn: 先写 screenplay，再画 storyboard，然后开机拍摄，顺序就是记忆顺序。

normal.en: A teleplay is for television, a screenplay is for the cinema screen.
normal.cn: teleplay 给电视，screenplay 给影院银幕，前半截成分决定了屏幕大小。

normal.en: An award for best original screenplay honours writing done without a book behind it.
normal.cn: 最佳原创剧本奖，表彰没有原著蓝本、完全原创的电影写作。

abstract.en: Picture a single sheet divided into columns of action and speech, slowly turning into a lit picture on a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一张分成动作栏与台词栏的纸，慢慢变成墙上被照亮的一幅画面。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom where the same sheet is being marked in red for rhythm, not for grammar.
abstract.cn: 想象一间课堂上，同一张纸被红笔批改，改的不是语法而是节奏。

abstract.en: Picture a bookshop shelf where the sheet sits in a bound volume beside novels.
abstract.cn: 想象一家书店的架子，同一张纸已装订成册，与小说摆在一起。

examples.en: The director asked for a rewrite of the screenplay.
examples.cn: 导演要求重写这份电影剧本。

examples.en: Her original screenplay won the top writing award.
examples.cn: 她的原创剧本赢得了最高编剧奖。

examples.en: He adapted the novel into a screenplay over two summers.
examples.cn: 他用了两个夏天把这部小说改编成电影剧本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「银幕＋剧本」——先想一块亮起来的幕布，再想铺在桌上的那叠稿纸，两样一叠就是电影剧本。这只是拆词联想，与词源过程无关。

root: 英语复合词：screen（银幕，十五世纪指隔板、屏障，后指放映幕布）+ play（戏、戏剧文本）。二十世纪初电影取代舞台时合成新词，最初写作 screen play，后合并为一个词。

sensesIntro.en: Screenplay names the text a film is made from, then the craft and format, the adaptation it often is, its role as the blueprint, and finally the printed version read as a book.
sensesIntro.cn: screenplay 先指拍电影所用的文本，再指这门手艺与体例，指改编而来的版本，指影片的拍摄蓝本，最后指被当书阅读的出版剧本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a typed script lies open, action on the left and speech on the right, with shot notes in between.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份打字稿摊开着，左边写动作，右边写台词，中间夹着镜头批注。

branches.en: THE PRODUCTION: the written text is the plan that the cameras and the cutting room follow.
branches.cn: 制作线：这份书面文本就是摄影机和剪辑台所遵循的计划。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: the thing written gives its name to the job and to its standard layout.
branches.cn: 行当线：写出的成品把名字给了这一职业及其标准排版。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: a novel or true story is rewritten into the form a film needs.
branches.cn: 来源线：小说或真实故事被改写成电影所需的形态。

branches.en: THE PAGE: published scripts are read for themselves, with no camera needed.
branches.cn: 纸页线：出版的剧本可以脱离摄影机独立阅读。

branches.en: RANGE: the same text may be a shooting document, a book, or both at once.
branches.cn: 范围线：同一份文本既可以是拍摄文书，也可以是书，甚至同时是两者。

intro.en: Screenplay is a pure English compound; its pieces are screen and play, and the family grows along the screen- line.
intro.cn: screenplay 是纯英语复合词，两个构件是 screen 与 play，词族主要沿 screen- 这条线扩展。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, so no Latin root is claimed; only the Old French ancestor of screen is relevant to its history.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本土构词，不主张任何拉丁词根；其历史只与 screen 的古法语祖先有关。

items.meaning: the sheet on which a film is shown
items.example: Screen once meant a partition, then the cinema screen.
items.exampleCN: screen 先指隔板，后指影院银幕。

items.meaning: a drama, or the written text of one
items.example: Play supplies the dramatic side of the compound.
items.exampleCN: play 为这个复合词提供「戏」的成分。

items.meaning: the text written for a film
items.example: Screenplay joins the two halves into one profession word.
items.exampleCN: screenplay 把两个构件合成为一个行业词。

items.example: The combining form -writer forms screenwriter.
items.exampleCN: 组合成分 -writer 构成 screenwriter。

items.example: A screenwriter works with the director before shooting.
items.exampleCN: 电影编剧在开拍前与导演一起工作。

items.example: The suffix -writing forms screenwriting.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -writing 构成 screenwriting。

items.meaning: the craft of writing scripts for films
items.example: Screenwriting courses teach scene structure.
items.exampleCN: 电影编剧课程教授场景结构。

items.meaning: the written text of a play or film
items.example: Script is the shorter, more general word.
items.exampleCN: script 是更短、更通用的说法。

items.example: The combining form -board appears in storyboard.
items.exampleCN: 组合成分 -board 出现在 storyboard 中。

items.meaning: a set of drawings mapping the shots
items.example: A storyboard draws the shots that the screenplay describes.
items.exampleCN: 故事板把电影剧本描述的画面画出来。

definition_zh: 电影编剧；电影剧本作者
definition_en: a person who writes the script for a film, television programme, or other moving picture
core_image: 一个人坐在书桌前，把脑海里的一幕幕画面写成有台词、有动作的稿纸
scene: 电影拍到一半，导演发现男女主角的对白怎么看都不自然，于是把原作者叫到了片场。The director called the screenwriter back to the set to rewrite three scenes of dialogue.
sceneCN: 这里 screenwriter 是「电影编剧」（第 1 个义项：专门为电影撰写剧本的人）；句意：导演把电影编剧请回片场，重写三场对白戏。

pos.zh: 电影编剧；电影剧本作者
电视编剧；电视剧本作者

derivatives.zh: 基础词加动词后缀 -ing 构成动名词，义为「编剧工作；剧本创作」
由 screen 与 play「剧本」复合而成，义为「电影剧本」
基础词的第一部分，原义「银幕」，转指「电影」这一媒介
近义复合词，由 script「脚本」加 writer 构成，可泛指影视、广播等各类编剧

senses.title: The writer of a film script
senses.definition: a person whose job is to write the script, including scenes and dialogue, for a feature film
senses.definitionCN: 专门为电影撰写剧本（含场景与对白）为己任的人
senses.example: A good screenwriter makes every line of dialogue count.
senses.exampleCN: 好的电影编剧让每一句对白都有分量。
senses.why: The compound joins screen, the surface on which films are shown, to writer, so the word names the person who writes for the screen.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示「银幕」的 screen 与 writer 直接拼成，意思就是为银幕写作的人，所以先长出「电影编剧」这个义项。

senses.title: The plot architect
senses.definition: the person who decides the structure and turning points of a story before it is filmed
senses.definitionCN: 在拍摄前决定故事结构与转折点的人
senses.example: As the screenwriter, he mapped out the three acts on a whiteboard.
senses.exampleCN: 作为编剧，他在白板上规划出三幕结构。
senses.why: Because the script lists the order of events, the writer is also the one who builds the skeleton of the plot.
senses.whyCN: 剧本要按顺序列出事件，于是写剧本的人自然就成了搭建情节骨架的人，这就是结构义项的来源。

senses.title: The revision voice
senses.definition: the writer who revises or polishes an existing script during production
senses.definitionCN: 在制作过程中修改或润色已有剧本的编剧
senses.example: The studio brought in another screenwriter for a final polish.
senses.exampleCN: 制片厂又请了一位编剧来做最后润色。
senses.why: Screenwriting is word upon word rewriting, so the role extends to the person who keeps revising an existing draft.
senses.whyCN: 编剧本身就是一遍遍改字的工作，因此这个身份也延伸到制作中不断修改现有稿件的人。

senses.title: The television writer
senses.definition: a writer who creates scripts for television series or single dramas
senses.definitionCN: 为电视剧集或单本电视话剧撰写剧本的人
senses.example: She spent five years as a television screenwriter before moving to film.
senses.exampleCN: 她在转入电影界之前做了五年电视编剧。
senses.why: Screen now covers the small screen as well as the cinema, so the compound moved with the medium.
senses.whyCN: screen 如今也涵盖电视荧屏，这个词便随媒介一起扩展到了电视剧写作。

senses.title: A credited role
senses.definition: the named writing credit shown in the titles of a film or series
senses.definitionCN: 在片头或片尾字幕中出现的编剧署名
senses.example: His screenwriter credit appeared right after the director.
senses.exampleCN: 他的编剧署名紧跟在导演之后。
senses.why: A job title can turn into a credit line, so the word also names a position printed on screen.
senses.whyCN: 职位名称可以转化为一行字幕署名，所以这个词也指片中被印出来的职位。

senses.title: A career identity
senses.definition: the professional identity or calling of writing for the screen
senses.definitionCN: 以写影视剧本为业的职业身份或志向
senses.example: He calls himself a screenwriter even when no project is in production.
senses.exampleCN: 即使手上没有在拍的项目，他也自称编剧。
senses.why: English job nouns readily describe identity rather than a single act, and this one is no exception.
senses.whyCN: 英语职业名词很容易从「动作」转向「身份」，screenwriter 也可以用来表明一个人属于这一行。

intro.en: Screenwriter is a modern compound of screen, from a French word for a shield or fire-guard, and writer, from the Old English verb writan.
intro.cn: screenwriter 是近代复合词：screen 来自法语，本指挡板或遮火屏；writer 来自古英语动词 writan（刻写）。

items.en: Scrinium means a case for scrolls or books.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scrinium 指存放卷轴或书籍的匣子。

items.en: Escran is a screen for protection against heat or wind.
items.cn: 古法语 escran 指挡热或挡风的屏风。

items.en: Screen arrives in English as a protective panel.
items.cn: screen 在十四世纪进入英语，表示起保护作用的屏板。

items.en: Screen shifts to the surface on which pictures are projected.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，screen 转为投影画面的表面，即银幕。

items.en: Screenwriter is coined for writers who work for the cinema.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现 screenwriter，专门指为电影写作的人。

items.en: The term now covers film, television, and streaming drama alike.
items.cn: 如今这个词涵盖电影、电视与流媒体剧集。

note.en: Screenwriter belongs to the writer family and to the word field of film production roles.
note.cn: screenwriter 属于 writer 词族，也处在影视制作职位的义场里。

entries.definition: a person who writes scripts for films, radio, or television
entries.definitionCN: 编剧；脚本作者，词形相近且近义

entries.definition: the script of a film
entries.definitionCN: 电影剧本，与 screenwriter 共用 screen

entries.definition: the art or work of writing films
entries.definitionCN: 编剧工作；剧本创作

entries.definition: a person who writes plays for the theatre
entries.definitionCN: 剧作家，写成形式接近，专指写舞台剧的人

entries.definition: the written text of a film or play
entries.definitionCN: 剧本；脚本，是编剧写出的成品

entries.definition: a person who writes long fictional stories
entries.definitionCN: 小说家，同为写故事的人但媒介不同

entries.definition: the person who controls how a film is made
entries.definitionCN: 导演，与编剧合作的制作核心

entries.definition: a writer of drama
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧作家，属于同为写剧本的人的义场

normalIntro.en: Screenwriter is built from two ordinary English words, screen and writer, and the whole meaning sits right inside them.
normalIntro.cn: screenwriter 由 screen 和 writer 两个普通词直接拼成，意思就藏在字面里。

normal.en: Screen plus writer gives the person who writes for the screen.
normal.cn: screen 加 writer 就是为银幕写作的人。

normal.en: The plural is simply screenwriters, with no spelling change.
normal.cn: 复数只是加 s，写成 screenwriters，拼写不变。

normal.en: Scriptwriter is the broader twin, used for radio and television too.
normal.cn: scriptwriter 是更宽泛的同门词，广播与电视也用。

normal.en: A screenwriter writes what actors later say on camera.
normal.cn: 编剧写下演员之后在镜头前说出的台词。

normal.en: Compare playwright: playwright is for the stage, screenwriter for the screen.
normal.cn: 对比 playwright：后者写给舞台，screenwriter 写给银幕。

abstract.en: Picture a blank page slowly filling with scene headings.
abstract.cn: 想象一页白纸上慢慢写满场景标题。

abstract.en: See the writer sitting inside a cinema screen like a frame.
abstract.cn: 想象写作者坐在银幕之内，像被画框框住。

abstract.en: Imagine your own life as a script you are drafting.
abstract.cn: 把自己的人生想成正在起草的剧本。

examples.en: The screenwriter won an award for the dialogue in the first act.
examples.cn: 这位电影编剧凭借第一幕的对白获奖。

examples.en: Many screenwriters work for months before a single scene is filmed.
examples.cn: 许多编剧在开机拍摄任何一场戏之前要工作数月。

examples.en: She wants to be a screenwriter rather than a novelist.
examples.cn: 她想当电影编剧，而不是小说家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯克林瑞特」——把银幕上的故事重新「瑞特」（write）一遍，就是编剧；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: screen（法语 escran 屏风 → 银幕，指电影媒介）+ writer（古英语 writan 刻写 → 写作者）；复合义「为银幕写作的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Screenwriter begins with the film writer, then extends to the plot builder, the reviser, the television writer, the credit line, and the career identity.
sensesIntro.cn: screenwriter 先指为电影写剧本的人，再扩展为情节设计者、改稿者、电视编剧、字幕署名直至职业身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a writer filling a blank page with scenes for the screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：写作者把一幕幕场景填满银幕用的空白页。

branches.en: The film writer is the central sense.
branches.cn: 电影编剧是中心义项。

branches.en: Building story structure is the architect role.
branches.cn: 搭建故事结构属于设计者角色。

branches.en: Revisions end in a printed credit line.
branches.cn: 不断改稿最终落到一行署名上。

branches.en: The television writer extends the medium.
branches.cn: 电视编剧是媒介的横向延伸。

branches.en: The job becomes an identity people claim.
branches.cn: 这份工作会变成人们自我认同的身份。

intro.en: Screenwriter is a pure English compound whose parts, screen and writer, are ordinary words with their own histories.
intro.cn: screenwriter 是纯粹的英语复合词，两个部分 screen 与 writer 都是自带历史来源的普通词。

latinIntro.en: Latin scrinium, a book case, went through French and Old English to supply both halves of this modern word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scrinium（书匣）经法语与古英语演变，为这个现代复合词提供了两部分来源。

items.meaning: a flat surface for showing pictures
items.example: Screen names the medium of film.
items.exampleCN: screen 指电影这一媒介。

items.meaning: a look-alike onset in scroll and scrollwork
items.meaningCN: 与 scroll 等词形似的开头
items.example: The sc- onset appears in many unrelated words.
items.exampleCN: sc- 开头出现在很多互不同源的词里。

items.example: Writer is built on the verb write.
items.exampleCN: writer 由动词 write 加 -er 构成。

items.example: Write comes from Old English writan.
items.exampleCN: write 来自古英语 writan。

items.meaning: a person who does an action
items.example: The suffix -er turns write into writer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把 write 变成 writer。

items.example: Playwright uses the older suffix -wright.
items.exampleCN: playwright 用的是更古老的 -wright 词尾。

items.example: Screenplay joins screen and play.
items.exampleCN: screenplay 由 screen 与 play 复合。

items.example: Screenwriting adds -ing to screenwrite.
items.exampleCN: screenwriting 由 screenwrite 加 -ing。

items.example: Scriptwriter uses script instead of screen.
items.exampleCN: scriptwriter 用 script 替换了 screen。

latinEntries.meaning: a case for books or scrolls

definition_zh: 编剧；脚本作者；剧本撰写人
definition_en: a person who writes scripts for films, television, radio, or advertisements
core_image: 一张被反复改过的脚本稿，左边一行写着动作，右边一行写着台词
scene: 广播剧开录前，制作人发现演员把两段台词读反了，需要有人当场修改脚本。The producer asked the scriptwriter to change the lines on the spot before recording.
sceneCN: 这里 scriptwriter 泛指「脚本作者」（第 2 个义项：为广播、电视等撰写脚本的人）；句意：制作人请脚本作者在录音前当场修改台词。

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「脚本创作」
基础词第一部分，义为「脚本；剧本」
由 screen「银幕」加 writer 构成，专指影视编剧，与 scriptwriter 常混用
与 writer 同源的动词，义为「书写」

senses.title: The film script writer
senses.definition: a person who writes the script of a film
senses.definitionCN: 为电影撰写剧本的人
senses.example: The scriptwriter turned the novel into a two-hour film.
senses.exampleCN: 这位编剧把小说改成了两小时的电影。
senses.why: Script first means a written text for performance, and writer names the person, so the compound means the one who writes that text.
senses.whyCN: script 本指供表演使用的文字文本，加 writer 表示做这件事的人，因此先得到「为电影写剧本的人」这一义项。

senses.title: The broadcast writer
senses.definition: a person who writes scripts for radio, television, or other non-cinema media
senses.definitionCN: 为广播、电视等非电影媒介撰写脚本的人
senses.example: Radio plays depend on a scriptwriter who can suggest pictures with sound.
senses.exampleCN: 广播剧依赖能用声音构想画面的脚本作者。
senses.why: Radio and television need a written plan too, so this general word covers them before film ever appears.
senses.whyCN: 广播和电视同样需要文字规划，因此这个宽泛的字面词先覆盖这些媒介，与电影无关。

senses.title: The advertising writer
senses.definition: a writer who creates the running ideas and lines for short advertisements
senses.definitionCN: 为短广告撰写创意与台词的人
senses.example: The agency keeps a scriptwriter for its thirty-second spots.
senses.exampleCN: 这家广告公司配了一位编剧专做三十秒短片。
senses.why: A commercial is a tiny scripted performance, so the same compound stretches to selling.
senses.whyCN: 广告就是一段极短的脚本表演，于是同一个复合词也延伸到了商业领域。

senses.title: The adapter
senses.definition: a writer who turns an existing novel, play, or true story into a script
senses.definitionCN: 把已有小说、戏剧或真实故事改写成剧本的人
senses.example: Finding the right scriptwriter is the hardest part of any adaptation.
senses.exampleCN: 找到合适的改编编剧是任何改编中最难的一步。
senses.why: Because a script must reshape a source text, the role also names the shaper of other stories.
senses.whyCN: 剧本必须重新组织源文本，因此这个身份也指把别处故事改写成剧本的人。

senses.title: The writing credit
senses.definition: the job title shown in the credits of a production
senses.definitionCN: 制作字幕中出现的编剧职位名
senses.example: The end titles list two scriptwriters for the series.
senses.exampleCN: 片尾字幕为这部系列剧列出两位编剧。
senses.why: Like other job nouns, it can appear as a plain name board rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 和其他职业名词一样，它也能只作为一块职位名牌出现在字幕上，而不指具体的人。

senses.title: A professional identity
senses.definition: the professional label people use to describe their career
senses.definitionCN: 人们用来描述自己职业的标签
senses.example: He calls himself a scriptwriter because it sounds broader than screenwriter.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称脚本作者，因为这样听起来比电影编剧更宽泛。
senses.why: The general first half of the compound makes it a comfortable umbrella identity.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词前半部分足够宽泛，因此很适合当作涵盖面更广的职业身份。

intro.en: Scriptwriter combines script, from Latin scribere, to write, with writer, from Old English writan, so both halves mean writing.
intro.cn: scriptwriter 由 script（源自拉丁语 scribere，书写）与 writer（源自古英语 writan，刻写）组成，两部分都表示「写」。

items.en: Scribere means to write, and scriptum means something written.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scribere 意为书写，scriptum 意为写下的东西。

items.en: Scrinium, a case for scrolls, may share an older root with the writing words.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scrinium（卷轴匣）一般认为与这些「书写」词共享更早的来源。

items.en: Scriptum narrows to a learner-written text.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中 scriptum 收窄为手写或抄写的文本。

items.en: Script enters English for written text and handwriting.
items.cn: script 在十四世纪进入英语，表示书面文本与手迹。

items.en: Script is applied to the written words of a play or film.
items.cn: 十九世纪 script 被用来指戏剧或电影的文字稿。

items.en: Scriptwriter is coined by replacing screen with the older word script.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现 scriptwriter，即以更古老的 script 替换 screen。

note.en: Scriptwriter is a writer compound whose nearest neighbours are the film word screenwriter and the product word script.
note.cn: scriptwriter 是 writer 复合词，最近邻是电影领域的 screenwriter 与产品词 script。

entries.definition: a person who writes scripts for films
entries.definitionCN: 电影编剧，常与 scriptwriter 互换使用

entries.definition: the written text of a play or film
entries.definitionCN: 脚本；剧本，是本词的第一部分

entries.definitionCN: 广告文案，后缀相同但对象是文案

normal.en: Screenwriter and scriptwriter are close twins, film against everything else.

normal.en: The related job word is scriptwriting, the work itself.
normal.cn: 相关职业名词是 scriptwriting，指这项工作本身。

abstract.en: Picture two columns on a page: action on the left, speech on the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上两栏：左边动作，右边台词。

abstract.en: See a long strip of paper curling out of a typewriter.

abstract.en: Think of a director shouting for the script every time something changes.
abstract.cn: 想象每次有变动导演都喊着要脚本。

examples.en: Honors went to the scriptwriter and the lead actress.
examples.cn: 荣誉归于编剧和女主角。

examples.en: Scriptwriters often work on several projects at the same time.
examples.cn: 编剧常常同时做几个项目。

examples.en: The scriptwriter described the scene in three short lines.
examples.cn: 编剧用三行短句描述这场戏。

branches.en: Broadcast and advertising widen the medium.

branches.en: The job title becomes a printed credit.

branches.en: The broad word works well as a career label.

definition_zh: 用力擦洗；刷洗；擦掉；矮树丛；灌木林地；弃用；取消
definition_en: to rub something hard to clean it, or to cancel something planned
core_image: 两只手握着硬毛刷，在木板上用力来回搓，把污垢一条条刷掉
scene: 露营结束，锅底糊了一层黑，父亲蹲在河边用沙子和刷子把它刷干净。Father scrubbed the burnt pot with sand and a stiff brush until it shone.
sceneCN: 这里 scrub 是「用力刷洗」（第 1 个义项：用刷子反复搓洗物体）；句意：父亲用沙子和硬刷把烧糊的锅刷到发亮。

collocations.zh: 彻底清洗；术前刷手消毒

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -er 构成施动名词，义为「擦洗的人或器」，也指工业洗涤器
动词加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「擦洗」这一动作
名词加 -y 构成形容词，义为「灌木丛生的；矮小的」
与 land 复合，义为「灌木地带；矮灌林地」

senses.title: To rub hard to clean
senses.definition: to clean something by rubbing it hard with a brush, cloth, or the hands
senses.definitionCN: 用刷子、布或双手反复用力搓洗，使之干净
senses.example: She scrubbed the kitchen floor on her knees.
senses.exampleCN: 她跪在地上刷洗厨房地板。
senses.why: The oldest verb sense is rubbing something hard to wear it or clean it, so this everyday sense is the word in its plainest form.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最早的义项就是用力搓擦，因此「刷洗」是这个词最本分的用法，也是整个词义的起点。

senses.title: To remove by rubbing
senses.definition: to remove a mark, stain, or dirt by rubbing
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复搓擦把痕迹、污渍或污垢去掉
senses.example: He scrubbed the ink off his fingers with soap.
senses.exampleCN: 他用肥皂把手指上的墨水搓洗干净。
senses.why: If rubbing can clean, it can also take something away entirely, so the object of the rubbing becomes the thing removed.
senses.whyCN: 既然搓擦能清洁，它也能带走某些东西，于是被搓的对象就转成了被去掉的痕迹，于是长出这个义项。

senses.title: Low woody growth
senses.definition: low trees and bushes, or an area covered with them
senses.definitionCN: 低矮的树木与灌木，或覆盖着这类植物的地带
senses.example: The trail climbed through thick scrub before reaching the field.
senses.exampleCN: 小径穿过茂密的灌木丛，然后到达田野。
senses.why: This noun sense is often said to come from the stunted, rubbed-down look of low bushes, though the link with the verb is debated.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为这个名词义与矮小灌木那种被「搓低」的形态有关，但它与动词的关系仍有争议，所以只算联想。

senses.title: To call off a launch
senses.definition: to cancel or stop a space flight, event, or plan before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在太空飞行、活动或计划开始之前将其取消或中止
senses.example: Engineers decided to scrub the launch because of high winds.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师因大风决定取消这次发射。
senses.why: Space teams wipe a launch off the board the way a mark is scrubbed from a sheet, so wiping leads to cancelling in technical English.
senses.whyCN: 航天团队把发射从日程板上擦掉，就像擦去纸上的记号，于是「擦除」在技术英语里引申为「取消」。

senses.title: A hard wash
senses.definition: an act of washing or cleaning something by rubbing hard
senses.definitionCN: 用力搓洗、清洁某物的动作
senses.example: Give the pan a good scrub before you put it away.
senses.exampleCN: 把锅好好刷一遍再收起来。
senses.why: Every English verb of cleaning yields a matching noun for the act, and the same shift happens here.
senses.whyCN: 英语中表示清洁的动词几乎都能转化为表示该动作的名词，scrub 也经历了同样的转换，因此有了这个义项。

senses.title: Very small or poor
senses.definition: used of animals or things that are undersized or of poor quality
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容动物或物品体格矮小或质量低劣
senses.example: A scrub bull had wandered into the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 一头瘦小的公牛游荡进了院子。
senses.why: Small, runty beasts are compared to low scrubby growth, so the plant sense lends its size to animals and goods.
senses.whyCN: 瘦小、发育不良的家畜被比作长不高的灌丛，于是植物义把「矮小」的特征借给了动物与物品。

senses.title: The wash-up before surgery
senses.definition: the careful washing of hands and arms by a surgeon or nurse before an operation
senses.definitionCN: 外科医生或护士在手术前对双手和手臂进行的仔细清洗
senses.example: The surgeon scrubbed up for ten minutes before entering the theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在进入手术室前刷手消毒了十分钟。
senses.why: Medical staff need the title dirt gone completely, so the plain verb is specialized into a formal washing ritual.
senses.whyCN: 医护人员需要彻底清除病菌，于是普通动词被专业化成一套正式的清洗程序，这就是这个义项的由来。

intro.en: The origin of scrub is uncertain; it is generally linked to Middle Low German or Middle Dutch words for rubbing, with the plant sense perhaps a separate development.
intro.cn: scrub 的来源不确定：一般认为与中低地德语或中古荷兰语中表示「搓擦」的词有关，植物义可能是另一条独立的发展线。

items.en: Most scholars reconstruct a Germanic root for rubbing or scouring.
items.cn: 大多数学者重构出一个表示「搓擦、擦洗」的日耳曼语词根（重构形式）。

items.en: Related forms in Middle Dutch mean to rub or curry an animal.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语中的相关词形表示擦搓或刷洗牲口。

items.en: Middle Low German supplies a parallel verb for hard rubbing.
items.cn: 中低地德语提供了表示用力擦洗的平行动词。

items.en: Scrub is first recorded in English with strong washing and scouring senses.
items.cn: scrub 在英语中最早见于表示强烈刷洗的用法，约在十四至十五世纪。

items.en: Debated link: scrub as low bushes may echo a separate northern word for stunted growth.
items.cn: 存疑之处：一般猜测表示矮灌木的 scrub 可能来自北方另一个表示「长不高」的词。

items.en: The spaceflight sense of cancelling a launch dates from about the nineteen fifties.
items.cn: 表示取消发射的航天用法大体出现在二十世纪五十年代。

note.en: Scrub sits near other rubbing verbs such as scour and rub, and near the plant word shrub.
note.cn: scrub 与 scour、rub 等「搓擦」动词相邻，也与植物词 shrub 容易混淆。

entries.definition: a small woody plant
entries.definitionCN: 灌木，只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person or machine that scrubs
entries.definitionCN: 擦洗的人或机器，是本词的派生词

entries.definition: covered with low bushes or looking small and poor
entries.definitionCN: 灌木丛生的；矮小寒酸的

entries.definition: to write or draw quickly and carelessly
entries.definitionCN: 乱写乱画，发音相近但词源不同

entries.definition: to clean a surface by rubbing it hard
entries.definitionCN: 擦净；刷净，与 scrub 几乎同义

entries.definition: to move your hand over something with pressure
entries.definitionCN: 摩擦；搓，是更宽泛的上位词

entries.definition: to make a surface smooth and shiny by rubbing
entries.definitionCN: 打亮；抛光，目的在光亮而非去污

entries.definition: to clean or tidy something with a brush
entries.definitionCN: 刷；用刷子清理，力度更轻

normalIntro.en: Scrub is a short, hard-sounding word, and the stiff br inside echoes the friction of a brush.
normalIntro.cn: scrub 又短又硬，中间的 br 读起来正像刷子在摩擦。

normal.en: Scrub doubled with a consonant: scrubbed, scrubbing, both take double b.
normal.cn: scrub 加词尾要双写 b：scrubbed 与 scrubbing。

normal.en: Scrub up means to scrub your hands clean, especially before surgery.
normal.cn: scrub up 指刷手消毒，尤其指手术前。

normal.en: Scrub the launch is aerospace jargon for calling it off.
normal.cn: scrub the launch 是航天行话，意为取消发射。

normal.en: Compare shrub: shrub is a plant, scrub can name both the plant and the rubbing.
normal.cn: 对比 shrub：shrub 只是植物，scrub 兼指植物与搓洗。

normal.en: The agent noun is scrubber, as in a back scrubber for the shower.
normal.cn: 施动名词是 scrubber，如洗澡用的搓背器。

abstract.en: Picture suds turning grey as the brush moves in circles.
abstract.cn: 想象泡沫随刷子转圈变灰。

abstract.en: Imagine a red stain fading to nothing on white tiles.
abstract.cn: 想象白瓷砖上的红渍渐渐消失。

abstract.en: See a countdown clock on a launch pad being wiped clean.
abstract.cn: 想象发射台上倒计时的钟面被人擦干净。

examples.en: You will have to scrub the sink before the guests arrive.
examples.cn: 客人来之前你得把水槽刷干净。

examples.en: They scrubbed the contaminated data from the disk.
examples.cn: 他们把受污染的数据从硬盘上清除掉。

examples.en: The wind forced the team to scrub the mission at the last minute.
examples.cn: 大风迫使团队在最后一刻取消任务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯克拉布」——拿起抹布（近似读作 bra）用力来回搓，就是刷洗；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：一般认为与日耳曼语表示「搓擦、擦洗」的词根有关（中古荷兰语与中低地德语有平行词形），植物义可能另有来源。

sensesIntro.en: Scrub moves from hard rubbing for cleanliness, to removing marks, to low bushes and small things, to cancelling a launch, and finally to the medical wash.
sensesIntro.cn: scrub 从用力搓洗出发，先引申为擦掉痕迹，再长成矮灌木与「矮小」，又派生为取消发射与术前刷手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stiff brush moving back and forth until the dirt is gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬毛刷来回搓动，直到污垢消失。

branches.en: The cleaning action and its noun stand together.
branches.cn: 清洁动作与其名词义项成对出现。

branches.en: Removing a mark is rubbing with an object taken away.
branches.cn: 擦掉痕迹就是搓走某个对象。

branches.en: Cancelling a launch is wiping it from the plan.
branches.cn: 取消发射就是把计划从日程上擦掉。

branches.en: Low bushes lend their size to undersized animals.
branches.cn: 矮灌木把「矮」借给了瘦小的动物。

branches.en: The surgical wash is the plain verb made a ritual.
branches.cn: 术前刷手消毒是普通动词仪式化的结果。

intro.en: Scrub is a short Germanic verb with few parts, and its family grows through the suffixes -er and -y and the compound -land.
intro.cn: scrub 是结构简短的日耳曼语动词，词族主要通过 -er、-y 后缀与 -land 复合来扩展。

latinIntro.en: Scrub has no reliable Latin source, so the Latin family here is limited to unrelated but useful writing and rubbing words.
latinIntro.cn: scrub 没有可靠的拉丁语来源，因此这里列出的拉丁同源条目只限于虽不同源但有用的书写与摩擦类词。

items.example: Scrub is the base form.
items.exampleCN: scrub 是基础形式。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does an action
items.example: The suffix -er forms scrubber.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 scrubber。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms scrubbing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 scrubbing。

items.example: The suffix -y forms scrubby.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 scrubby。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
items.example: Scrub doubles the b before -ed.
items.exampleCN: scrub 在加 -ed 前要双写 b。

items.meaning: a person or machine that scrubs
items.example: A scrubber removes gas from chimneys.
items.exampleCN: 洗涤器用于清除烟囱气体。

items.example: Scrubbing the deck took all morning.
items.exampleCN: 刷洗甲板花了一上午。

items.example: Scrubby hills rose behind the town.
items.exampleCN: 小镇后面是灌木丛生的山丘。

items.example: Scrubland survives long dry seasons.
items.exampleCN: 灌木地带能熬过长旱季。

definition_zh: 顾虑；顾忌；一丝良知上的不安；极小的量（旧用法）
definition_en: a moral doubt or hesitation that stops you from doing something you think may be wrong, or a very small amount of something
core_image: 手停在半空：一颗小石子硌在鞋底，脚下迟疑了一下
scene: 买家的报价低得离谱，可他还是签了字，事后连一点良心上的不安都没有。He signed the unfair contract without a scruple.
sceneCN: 这里 scruple 是「良心上的顾虑」（第 1 个义项：觉得不妥而迟疑）；句意：他签下不公平的合同，却毫无良心上的不安。

pos.zh: 顾虑；顾忌；良知上的不安
极小的量（旧用法，如一点盐）
对做某事有顾虑；犹豫（常用否定式）

collocations.zh: 毫不犹豫地去做；毫无顾忌地去做

derivatives.zh: 由 scruple 加 -ous 构成，义为「一丝不苟的；有良知的」
scrupulous 加 -ly 构成，义为「一丝不苟地；毫无例外地」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「无所顾忌的；不择手段的」
unscrupulous 加 -ly 构成，义为「肆无忌惮地」
稀有写法，加 -less 构成，义为「毫无顾忌的」

senses.title: A moral doubt that makes you hesitate
senses.definition: a feeling of doubt about whether something is morally right, which makes you hesitate to do it
senses.definitionCN: 怀疑某事在道德上是否正当，因而犹豫不敢去做的那份不安
senses.example: She had no scruples about firing the oldest worker.
senses.exampleCN: 她对解雇那位最年长的员工毫无顾虑。
senses.why: The Latin root is a small sharp stone: a scruple is a tiny grit in the mind that rubs and makes the will pause.
senses.whyCN: 词根原指一颗尖利的小石子；所谓顾虑，就是心里硌着的一粒小砂，磨得人步子一顿。

senses.title: Reluctance shown by a verb
senses.definition: to hesitate or be unwilling because you think an action may be wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因认为某个行为可能不正当而迟疑、不愿去做
senses.example: He did not scruple to lie when it suited him.
senses.exampleCN: 只要对他有利，他撒谎时从不迟疑。
senses.why: From the noun grew a verb: to have a scruple became to scruple, and it survives mostly in the negative, did not scruple to do.
senses.whyCN: 名词长出了动词：心里有顾虑，就成了迟疑不敢做；这个动词如今多用在否定句里，如「毫不迟疑地去做」。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: an extremely small quantity of something, as in an old unit of weight or a tiny pinch of an ingredient
senses.definitionCN: 极其微小的量，旧时指很小的称量单位，也指配料里的一小撮
senses.example: Add a scruple of salt to the water.
senses.exampleCN: 往水里加一丝盐。
senses.why: A scruple was also a tiny apothecaries weight, about twenty grains, so the word came to mean the smallest pinch of anything.
senses.whyCN: scruple 曾是药剂师用的一种极小重量单位，约二十格令，于是这个词又转指任何东西的一小撮。

intro.en: Scruple comes from Latin scrupulus, a small sharp stone, through the idea of a grit in the mind that makes one hesitate.
intro.cn: scruple 源自拉丁语 scrupulus（尖利的小石子），经由「心里硌着一粒砂而踌躇」这一比喻而来。

items.en: Scrupulus is a diminutive of scrupus, a sharp little stone.
items.cn: scrupulus 是 scrupus（尖利小石）的指小形式。

items.en: Cicero already uses scrupulus for a small uneasy doubt.
items.cn: 西塞罗已用 scrupulus 表示心头小小的不安与疑虑。

items.en: The word also names a very small apothecaries weight.
items.cn: 该词同时指药剂师所用的一种极小重量单位。

items.en: Scrupule carries the doubt sense into French.
items.cn: scrupule 带着「顾虑」之义进入法语。

items.en: English scruple first means a small unit of weight, then a moral doubt.
items.cn: 英语 scruple 先指小重量单位，再指良心上的不安。

items.en: The doubt sense widens into the everyday plural scruples.
items.cn: 「顾虑」之义扩展为日常常用的复数 scruples。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the scr- opening, while the near-meaning group gathers words for conscience, restraint, and a tiny amount.
note.cn: 形近组共享 scr- 开头；近义组则汇集表示良心、自我克制与微小数量的词。

entries.definition: careful and honest to the smallest detail
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，同根，义为「一丝不苟的；有良知的」

entries.definition: in a careful and honest way
entries.definitionCN: 副词，同根，义为「一丝不苟地」

entries.definition: close and searching examination
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同：scrutiny 源自拉丁语 scrutari（搜寻），义为「细查」

entries.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong
entries.definitionCN: 近义，指内心的是非感「良心」，是顾虑的来源

entries.definition: a brief feeling of doubt or unease
entries.definitionCN: 近义，指一阵短暂的不安或疑虑

entries.definition: a slight feeling of guilt
entries.definitionCN: 近义，指内疚；与 scruple 常在同一语境里互换

normalIntro.en: Scruple is a small stone in the mind: the grit that arrests the hand before a questionable act.
normalIntro.cn: scruple 是心里的一粒小石子：正是这粒砂让手在可疑之事前停住。

normal.en: The Latin scrupulus is a tiny sharp stone, the source of both the doubt and the small amount.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 scrupulus 是一颗尖利的小石子，既是「顾虑」又是「微量」的来源。

normal.en: Without scruple means with no moral hesitation at all.
normal.cn: without scruple 表示毫无良心上的迟疑。

normal.en: Scruples is almost always plural when it names moral doubts.
normal.cn: 表示道德顾虑时几乎总用复数 scruples。

normal.en: Scrupulous and unscrupulous grow from scruple, one careful, one careless of right and wrong.
normal.cn: scrupulous 与 unscrupulous 都从 scruple 长出来，一个讲原则，一个不顾是非。

normal.en: Compare with scrutiny: same scr- start, but one is a moral stone and the other a search.
normal.cn: 与 scrutiny 对比：同样以 scr- 开头，但一个指心里的小石子，一个指搜寻。

abstract.en: Picture a hand frozen over a contract as a grain of sand grinds under the heel.
abstract.cn: 想象手握在合同上方停住，同时鞋底硌着一粒砂。

abstract.en: Imagine a voice that asks only for a moment before doing something dishonest.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音，只要求在做出不诚实的事之前，给你片刻的停顿。

abstract.en: Think of a minute set of brass weights used for a pinch of powder.
abstract.cn: 想象一副称量一小撮粉末的微型铜砝码。

examples.en: The company hired a lawyer with no scruples about bending the rules.
examples.cn: 公司聘用了一位对钻空子毫无顾忌的律师。

examples.en: He would not scruple to break a promise if it saved the firm.
examples.cn: 只要能保住公司，他打破承诺也不会迟疑。

examples.en: A scruple of doubt stopped her from signing the letter.
examples.cn: 一丝疑虑让她没有在信上签字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死顾虑」——想得太死，顾虑太重；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 scrupus（尖利小石）→ 指小形式 scrupulus（小石子）→ 比喻心里硌着的「小疑虑」→ 古法语 scrupule → 英语 scruple，核心义「心里的一粒砂」。

sensesIntro.en: Scruple starts as a moral doubt, extends to the verb that expresses hesitation, and keeps an older sense of a tiny weight.
sensesIntro.cn: scruple 从「良心上的顾虑」出发，延伸出表示迟疑的动词用法，又保留了「极小重量」这一旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grain of stone that makes the hand stop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒硌手的小石子，让伸出的手停住。

branches.en: The moral doubt is the central everyday sense.
branches.cn: 道德层面上的顾虑是日常最核心的义项。

branches.en: The verb carries the same unease into action.
branches.cn: 动词义把同样的不安带进了动作层面。

branches.en: The tiny weight keeps the literal stone meaning alive.
branches.cn: 「极小重量」让字面上的小石子之义得以留存。

branches.en: Both a moral scruple and a scruple of powder are very small things with force.
branches.cn: 道德顾虑与一撮粉末都是微小却起作用的东西。

branches.en: A scruple is the feeling and to scruple is the act it produces.
branches.cn: scruple 既是那份感受，也是它促使的迟疑行为。

intro.en: Scruple is a Latin diminutive built on the stone scrupus, with English kin like scrupulous and unscrupulous.
intro.cn: scruple 是建立在「石头」scrupus 之上的拉丁语指小词，英语中围绕它构成 scrupulous 与 unscrupulous 等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin scrupus means a sharp stone and scrupulus its little form; scrupulum also names a small weight.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scrupus 意为尖利之石，scrupulus 是其指小形式；scrupulum 又指一种小重量单位。

items.example: Scrupus supplies the picture of the grit.
items.exampleCN: scrupus 提供了硌脚小石子的画面。

items.meaning: a little stone, a small doubt
items.example: The -ulus ending marks the diminutive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ulus 表示指小。

items.example: This unit gives the sense of a very small amount.
items.exampleCN: 这一单位提供了「微量」的意思。

items.example: Scruple keeps the noun sense of doubt.
items.exampleCN: scruple 保留表示疑虑的名词义。

items.example: To scruple is mostly used in negative sentences.
items.exampleCN: 表示迟疑的动词多用于否定句。

items.example: The suffix -ous makes scrupulous from scruple.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把 scruple 变成 scrupulous。

items.example: The prefix un- turns scrupulous into unscrupulous.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 scrupulous 变成 unscrupulous。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms scrupulously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 scrupulously。

items.example: The suffix -less forms the rare scrupleless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成罕见的 scrupleless。

latinEntries.meaning: a little stone, a small doubt

definition_zh: 一丝不苟的；极其细心的；有良知的；讲究道德的
definition_en: very careful to do everything correctly and honestly, or very careful about details
core_image: 戴着白手套的人一寸寸擦着玻璃，连最边角也不肯放过
scene: 这位会计把每一个数字都核对了两遍，做事极其一丝不苟。The accountant was scrupulous about every number.
sceneCN: 这里 scrupulous 是「一丝不苟的」（第 1 个义项：极其细心、不肯马虎）；句意：这位会计对每个数字都一丝不苟。

pos.zh: 一丝不苟的；极其细心的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「一丝不苟地」
加 -ness 构成，义为「一丝不苟；严谨」
加 un- 构成，义为「无所顾忌的；不择手段的」
由拉丁形式派生的 -osity 名词，义为「过分拘谨；病态的顾虑」

senses.title: Extremely careful about detail
senses.titleCN: 一丝不苟的；极其细心的
senses.definition: taking great care to do every part of a task correctly, including the smallest details
senses.definitionCN: 极其用心地做好每件事，连最小的细节也不放过
senses.example: She kept scrupulous records of every payment.
senses.exampleCN: 她把每一笔付款都记录得一丝不苟。
senses.why: The root is a sharp little stone, so a scrupulous person is one who cannot bear a single grit in the work.
senses.whyCN: 词根是尖利的小石子；scrupulous 就是容不下作品里哪怕一粒砂的人。

senses.title: Honest and morally exact
senses.definition: very careful not to do anything dishonest, unfair, or morally wrong
senses.definitionCN: 极其谨慎，绝不做不诚实、不公正或有违道德的事
senses.example: He is scrupulous in his dealings with clients.
senses.exampleCN: 他与客户往来时非常讲原则。
senses.why: The parent noun scruple is a moral doubt, so the adjective also describes someone who will not step over a line.
senses.whyCN: 母词 scruple 指道德上的顾虑；因此这个形容词也形容不肯越雷池半步的人。

intro.en: Scrupulous is Latin scrupulosus, full of small sharp stones, built on scrupulus, a little stone, with the suffix -ous.
intro.cn: scrupulous 来自拉丁语 scrupulosus（满是尖利小石），由 scrupulus（小石子）加词尾 -ous 构成。

items.en: Scrupulus is a little sharp stone, often used for a nagging doubt.
items.cn: scrupulus 指尖利的小石子，常用来比喻揪心的疑虑。

items.en: The suffix -osus adds the idea of being full of something.
items.cn: 词尾 -osus 表示「充满……」。

items.en: Scrupulosus means full of care, fussy, exact.
items.cn: scrupulosus 意为极为精细、谨小慎微。

items.en: The word enters French as scrupuleux.
items.cn: 该词以 scrupuleux 的形式进入法语。

items.en: English adopts it for meticulous and morally careful behavior.
items.cn: 英语借入后用来形容细致严谨、注重道义的行为。

items.en: Unscrupulous, its opposite, becomes common in business writing.
items.cn: 其反义词 unscrupulous 在商业写作中变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the scrup- stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for care and exactness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 scrup- 词干；近义组汇集表示细心与精确的词。

entries.definition: a moral doubt about doing something
entries.definitionCN: 同根，名词，义为「良心上的顾虑」

entries.definition: in a very careful and honest way
entries.definitionCN: 派生副词，义为「一丝不苟地」

entries.definition: willing to be dishonest in order to get what one wants
entries.definitionCN: 同根反义，义为「不择手段的」

entries.definition: showing great attention to small details
entries.definitionCN: 近义，指对细节极为讲究（偏重细节层面）

entries.definition: careful to follow rules and customs exactly
entries.definitionCN: 近义且正式，指对礼数与规矩一丝不差

entries.definition: working hard and doing what is right out of duty
entries.definitionCN: 近义，指凭责任心认真做事；与「讲究道德」之意最贴近

normalIntro.en: Scrupulous is scruple plus -ous: a person so full of small scruples that no detail and no dishonest gain escapes notice.
normalIntro.cn: scrupulous 就是 scruple 加 -ous：心里装满了小小的顾虑，既不放过一个细节，也不放过一点不义之财。

normal.en: Scrupulous about something means unwilling to do it carelessly or wrongly.
normal.cn: be scrupulous about sth 表示对某事绝不肯马虎或出错。

normal.en: The pair scrupulous and unscrupulous shows how un- reverses the moral sense.
normal.cn: scrupulous 与 unscrupulous 成对出现，可见 un- 如何反转道德含义。

normal.en: Scrupulously often modifies checked, recorded, and observed.
normal.cn: scrupulously 常修饰核对、记录与遵守这类动作。

normal.en: For grammar, use more and most, never scrupulouser.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more 与 most，绝不说 scrupulouser。

normal.en: Compare meticulous for detail and conscientious for duty, both close to scrupulous.
normal.cn: 对比 meticulous（重细节）与 conscientious（重责任），二者都与 scrupulous 相近。

abstract.en: Picture a gloved hand wiping the very corners of a window until it squeaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只戴白手套的手把窗角擦到吱吱作响。

abstract.en: Imagine a person who returns a coin found in the street to a stranger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在街上捡到硬币，非要还给陌生人。

abstract.en: Think of a wall of tiny pebbles: one wrong stone and the whole row looks off.
abstract.cn: 想象一面小石子砌成的墙：只要一块放歪了，整排看着就不对。

examples.en: The team kept a scrupulous account of where the money went.
examples.cn: 团队对资金的去向记了一笔一丝不苟的账。

examples.en: She is scrupulous about not taking credit for other people ideas.
examples.cn: 她一向不肯把别人的想法据为己有。

examples.en: Scrupulous checking caught the error before the report was printed.
examples.cn: 一丝不苟的核对在报告付印前发现了错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四颗快乐石」——四颗小石头都一一捡干净，做事一丝不苟；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 scrupus（尖利小石）+ 指小词尾 -ulus → scrupulus（小石子、小疑虑）→ scrupulosus（满是小石子，即极其精细）→ 古法语 scrupuleux → 英语 scrupulous，核心义「容不下一粒砂」。

sensesIntro.en: Scrupulous covers two faces of the same carefulness: exactness about details and exactness about right and wrong.
sensesIntro.cn: scrupulous 覆盖同一种谨慎的两面：对细节的精确，以及对是非的精确。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that will not leave one grain of grit behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只不肯留下一粒砂的手。

branches.en: Exactness about detail is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 对细节的讲究是日常义项。

branches.en: Exactness about morality grows from the same root.
branches.cn: 对道德的讲究出自同一词根。

branches.en: A careful auditor and a careful witness share the same scruple about error.
branches.cn: 认真的审计员与诚实的证人都对出错抱有同样的顾虑。

branches.en: This sense usually pairs with about, with, or attention to.
branches.cn: 此义常与 about、with 或 attention to 搭配。

branches.en: This sense edges into honesty and fair dealing.
branches.cn: 此义靠近诚实与公平交易的义场。

intro.en: Scrupulous is scruple with the adjective suffix -ous, and it anchors a family from scrupulously to unscrupulous.
intro.cn: scrupulous 是 scruple 加形容词词尾 -ous 构成，并维系着从 scrupulously 到 unscrupulous 的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scrupulus is a little stone, and the suffix -osus means full of, giving scrupulosus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scrupulus 意为小石子，词尾 -osus 表示充满，二者合成 scrupulosus。

items.meaning: a little stone, a small doubt
items.example: Scrupulus is the stem of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: scrupulus 是整个词族的词干。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.meaningCN: 表示充满或具有某种性质
items.example: The suffix -ous forms scrupulous from scruple.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把 scruple 变成 scrupulous。

items.example: The Latin suffix -osus gives scrupulosus.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁词尾 -osus 构成 scrupulosus。

items.example: Scrupulosus is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: scrupulosus 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms scrupulously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 scrupulously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms scrupulousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成名词 scrupulousness。
