items.meaningCN: 表示状态的拉丁系词尾
items.example: The form scrupulosity keeps the Latin ending.
items.exampleCN: scrupulosity 保留了拉丁词尾形式。

items.example: The prefix un- makes unscrupulous.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unscrupulous。

items.example: Scrupulously modifies verbs of checking.
items.exampleCN: scrupulously 常修饰核对类动词。

items.meaningCN: 无所顾忌的；不择手段的
items.example: Unscrupulous describes people who ignore scruples.
items.exampleCN: unscrupulous 形容无视顾虑的人。

latinEntries.meaning: a little stone, a small doubt

definition_zh: 仔细检查；仔细审视；详细研究
definition_en: to examine something very carefully and thoroughly, so that nothing is missed
core_image: 举着放大镜一寸寸扫过纸面，连纸纹都在光下现形
scene: 审计员逐条核对账目，花了好几个小时仔细翻查。The auditor spent hours scrutinizing every line of the accounts.
sceneCN: 这里 scrutinize 是「仔细检查」（第 1 个义项：逐项细看，不漏任何地方）；句意：审计员花了几个小时逐行细查账目。

pos.zh: 作细查；深入探究（较少用）

collocations.zh: 在显微镜下细查（喻追根究底地审视）

derivatives.zh: 由动词去 -ize 加 -y 构成，义为「细查；审视」
加 -er 构成，义为「细查者；审视者」
分词形容词化，义为「审视的；锐利的（目光）」
英式拼写，加 -isation 构成，义为「细查过程」

senses.title: To examine something thoroughly
senses.definition: to look at or go through something in a very close and systematic way, looking for hidden details or problems
senses.definitionCN: 以非常贴近而系统的方式逐处查看，寻找隐藏的细节或问题
senses.example: Customs officers scrutinized every bag in the queue.
senses.exampleCN: 海关人员逐件细查了队伍里的每个包。
senses.why: Latin scrutari means to search through rubbish or junk, so scrutinizing is a search that sifts everything, nothing skipped.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 scrutari 意为翻拣杂物；所谓细查，就是把东西一件件筛过，什么都不漏。

senses.title: To study or judge critically
senses.definition: to study something carefully in order to judge its quality, honesty, or worth
senses.definitionCN: 仔细研究某事，以评判其质量、真伪或价值
senses.example: Editors scrutinized the report before it went to print.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑们在报告付印前对它作了仔细审查。
senses.why: Once the searching gaze turns on a claim, the word also means testing it, so scrutiny becomes a judgment.
senses.whyCN: 当搜寻的目光落在某个说法上，这个词也就带上了检验之意，审视随之成为评判。

senses.title: To look at someone closely
senses.definition: to look at a person or thing with a sharp, searching gaze, as if reading what is there
senses.definitionCN: 用锐利而搜寻的目光盯住人或物看，仿佛要把一切读出来
senses.example: The professor scrutinized the newcomer over his glasses.
senses.exampleCN: 教授隔着眼镜细细打量这位新来的人。
senses.why: The physical search behind the word survives in the ordinary act of scanning a face for a clue.
senses.whyCN: 词源里翻拣搜寻的动作并未消失，只是变成了从一张脸上读出线索的日常举动。

intro.en: Scrutinize is built on Latin scrutari, to search, with the verb suffix -ize, and is tied to the noun scrutiny.
intro.cn: scrutinize 由拉丁语 scrutari（搜寻）加动词词尾 -ize 构成，与名词 scrutiny 同源。

items.en: Scruta means odds and ends, rubbish, the sort of pile that must be picked through.
items.cn: scruta 泛指杂物、破烂，是必须一件件翻拣的那堆东西。

items.en: Scrutari means to search through such a heap, and so to investigate.
items.cn: scrutari 意为在这类杂物堆里翻找，引申为查究。

items.en: Scrutinium is the act of searching; its origin from scruta is assumed by most scholars but not certain.
items.cn: scrutinium 指搜寻这一行为；其与 scruta 的关联为大多数学者所采纳，但并非确证。

items.en: Scrutiny names a careful examination or an assembly inquiry.
items.cn: scrutiny 指仔细检查，也指集会中的查问。

items.en: The verb scrutinize appears, formed on scrutiny with the suffix -ize.
items.cn: 动词 scrutinize 出现，以 scrutiny 为基加 -ize 构成。

items.en: British writing often spells it scrutinise, while American writing keeps the z.
items.cn: 英式写作常拼作 scrutinise，美式则保留字母 z。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the scrut- stem, while the near-meaning group gathers verbs of looking closely.
note.cn: 形近组共享 scrut- 词干；近义组汇集表示仔细查看的动词。

entries.definition: careful and searching examination
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，义为「细查；审视」

entries.definition: a person who examines things closely
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「细查者」

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same verb
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的英式拼写，读音完全相同

entries.definition: to look at something closely to check it
entries.definitionCN: 近义，指为了检查而查看（公务员用语最常用）

entries.definition: to look at something carefully in order to learn about it
entries.definitionCN: 近义，指为了了解而仔细查看（语气中性）

entries.definition: to read something in a thorough way
entries.definitionCN: 近义且正式，专指仔细通读文字材料

normalIntro.en: Scrutinize is scrutiny turned into an action: you take the pile apart until every piece has been seen.
normalIntro.cn: scrutinize 就是把 scrutiny 变成动作：把那一堆东西拆开，看清每一件。

normal.en: Scrutinize takes the noun scrutiny and adds -ize, meaning to do what the noun names.
normal.cn: scrutinize 由名词 scrutiny 加 -ize 而来，意即做出该名词所指的动作。

normal.en: The adverb closely almost always sits beside it, as in closely scrutinized.
normal.cn: 副词 closely 几乎总跟在它旁边，如 closely scrutinized。

normal.en: The British spelling with s, scrutinise, is equally correct.
normal.cn: 以 s 结尾的英式拼写 scrutinise 同样正确。

normal.en: Passive forms are common in news and law, as in the plan was scrutinized.
normal.cn: 新闻与法律文本中常用被动，如 the plan was scrutinized。

normal.en: Compare inspect for rules and check, examine for knowledge.
normal.cn: 对比 inspect（查合规）与 examine（求了解）。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass moving slowly until it spots a hairline crack.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜缓缓移动，直到映出一道发丝般的裂纹。

abstract.en: Imagine a reviewer reading a draft with a pencil, marking every doubtful phrase.
abstract.cn: 想象审稿人拿着铅笔读草稿，把每个可疑的措辞都圈出来。

abstract.en: Think of a sharp pair of eyes that never blink while a stranger walks past.
abstract.cn: 想象一双锐利的眼睛，在陌生人走过时连眨都不眨。

examples.en: Investors scrutinized the annual report for signs of trouble.
examples.cn: 投资者细细琢磨年报，寻找不利的迹象。

examples.en: Every application is scrutinized by two independent reviewers.
examples.cn: 每份申请都由两位独立评审仔细审查。

examples.en: She scrutinized his face, looking for the slightest hesitation.
examples.cn: 她盯着他的脸细看，想找出任何一丝迟疑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死搜特乃子」——死命地搜，一件都不漏，就是细查；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 scruta（杂物、破烂）→ scrutari（在杂物堆里翻找，即查究）→ scrutinium（搜寻）→ 英语 scrutiny → 加 -ize 得动词 scrutinize，核心义「一件件翻拣」。

sensesIntro.en: Scrutinize moves from a physical search through things, to a critical judging of claims, to a sharp gaze at people.
sensesIntro.cn: scrutinize 从对物品的翻拣细查，走到对说法的批判性评判，再到对人锐利的注视。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnifying glass sweeping every inch of the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：放大镜一寸寸扫过整页纸面。

branches.en: Thorough physical examination is the central sense.
branches.cn: 彻底的实体检查是核心义项。

branches.en: Turning the search on a claim yields the judging sense.
branches.cn: 把搜寻转向某个说法，就得到评判性的义项。

branches.en: The same search becomes a fixed stare at a person.
branches.cn: 同样的搜寻化为对人凝视不动的目光。

branches.en: An auditor examines records and passes judgement on them in one act.
branches.cn: 审计员在同一个动作里既细查账目，又对账目作出判断。

branches.en: Editors and interviewers both test what they see with a cool, inquiring look.
branches.cn: 编辑与面试官都用冷静探询的目光检验眼前所见。

intro.en: Scrutinize is the verb from scrutiny, built on Latin scrutari, and it heads a family that includes scrutinizer and scrutiny.
intro.cn: scrutinize 是由 scrutiny 派生的动词，建立在拉丁语 scrutari 之上，词族包含 scrutinizer 与 scrutiny。

latinIntro.en: Latin scruta means odds and ends, scrutari means to search through them, and scrutinium names the search.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scruta 意为杂物，scrutari 意为翻找这些杂物，scrutinium 则指这种搜寻。

items.example: Scruta supplies the heap that must be sifted.
items.exampleCN: scruta 提供了必须逐件筛拣的那堆东西。

items.example: Scrutari is the verb behind scrutiny.
items.exampleCN: scrutari 是 scrutiny 背后的动词。

items.example: Scrutinium becomes the English noun scrutiny.
items.exampleCN: scrutinium 变成英语名词 scrutiny。

items.example: Scrutiny is the base of the verb.
items.exampleCN: scrutiny 是动词的构词基础。

items.meaning: to make, to act in a way
items.example: The suffix -ize turns scrutiny into scrutinize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 把 scrutiny 变成 scrutinize。

items.meaningCN: 英式拼写变体，与 -ize 同义
items.example: The suffix -ise gives scrutinise in British English.
items.exampleCN: 英式英语用词尾 -ise 拼作 scrutinise。

items.example: The suffix -er forms scrutinizer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 scrutinizer。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示行为或状态的名词
items.example: The suffix -y forms scrutiny.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成名词 scrutiny。

items.example: The suffix -ation gives scrutinisation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 scrutinisation。

items.example: Scrutinizing describes a searching look.
items.exampleCN: scrutinizing 形容搜寻式的目光。

definition_zh: 仔细检查；细看；审视；审查
definition_en: careful and detailed examination of something, especially by other people who want to find out if it is right or honest
core_image: 一只手把纸页凑到灯下，眼睛逐行扫过，连边角的划痕都不放过
scene: 公司财报公布后，股东和记者都盯着那几行数字反复核对。The accounts of the firm came under close scrutiny after the audit.
sceneCN: 这里 scrutiny 是「仔细审查」（第 1 个义项：对文件、账目等逐项细查）；句意是审计之后，这家公司的账目受到严密审查。注意它常与 under 连用，说成 under scrutiny，强调被审视的状态。

pos.zh: 仔细检查；细看；审查：对事物或行为细致入微的察看与核查（不可数）

collocations.zh: 受到严密审查；处在细察之下
须接受审查；要经受审视

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「仔细检查；细看」
scrutinize 的英式拼写，义为「仔细检查；细看」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「仔细检查的人；审查者」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「爱刨根问底的；仔细探究的」

senses.title: A close and critical look
senses.definition: a careful, detailed look at something in order to judge its quality, truth or condition
senses.definitionCN: 为了判断质量、真伪或状况而对某物进行的细致察看
senses.example: The old maps came under close scrutiny by two historians.
senses.exampleCN: 两位历史学家仔细检视了这些旧地图。
senses.why: In Latin scrutari means to search through rags, ransacking rubbish for anything hidden; the eye of scrutiny is still that busy, digging search.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 scrutari 原指翻刨破布堆、在垃圾里搜找藏起来的东西；scrutiny 的目光仍是那种翻找不停的搜寻。

senses.title: Official investigation
senses.definition: a formal process in which an authority investigates something, often to check that rules were followed
senses.definitionCN: 官方机构对某事的正式调查，常为核查是否遵守规定
senses.example: The airline has been under official scrutiny since the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 那次坠机事故之后，这家航空公司一直受到官方审查。
senses.why: When the person who searches with care holds authority, the same act becomes an official investigation.
senses.whyCN: 当仔细翻查的人握有权力时，同一个行为就升级为正式调查。

senses.title: Public attention
senses.definition: the careful attention of the public or of newspapers, which notice every fault and comment on it
senses.definitionCN: 公众或媒体对某事的高度关注，会注意并评论每一个毛病
senses.example: The expenses of the minister were debated under heavy public scrutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 在公众的密切关注下，人们就部长的报销开支展开了争论。
senses.why: Thousands of careful eyes do the work that one person did in the first sense, so the public itself becomes the examiner.
senses.whyCN: 成千上万双仔细的眼睛替代了第一个义项里一个人的目光，于是公众本身成了检验者。

senses.title: Testing an idea against evidence
senses.definition: a repeated and critical testing of an idea, theory or evidence in order to see whether it holds
senses.definitionCN: 对观点、理论或证据反复提出质疑与检验，以判断其是否站得住
senses.example: Every claim in the paper has to withstand real scrutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 论文中的每一项主张都必须经得起真正的检验。
senses.why: An idea is treated like a pile of rags to be turned over: only what survives the careful turning is kept.
senses.whyCN: 观点被当成一堆要翻检的破布：凡是经得起仔细翻找的东西才被留下。

intro.en: Scrutiny descends from the Latin noun scrutinium, which comes from scrutor, to search through heaps, and ultimately from scruta, rags and rubbish.
intro.cn: scrutiny 来自拉丁语名词 scrutinium，其源头是动词 scrutor「翻找、搜查」，更早可追溯到 scruta，本义是破布与垃圾。

items.en: Plural of scrutum, meaning oddments, rags and worthless bits for sale; some sources describe the pile of broken goods sold in a heap.
items.cn: scrutum 的复数形式，指杂碎旧货、破布与卖不掉的零碎物品；有资料说它是整堆出售的破损杂货。

items.en: A verb meaning to search through, to ransack; the picture is of hands turning rubbish over to find the one thing worth keeping.
items.cn: 动词，意为翻找、搜查；画面是双手在垃圾堆里翻来翻去，只为找到值得留下的那一件东西。

items.en: A noun for a search or inquiry, and in Rome especially for the formal counting of votes one by one.
items.cn: 名词，指搜查、探究；在古罗马还专指把选票一张一张清点的正式查验。

items.en: The word enters French in the fourteenth century and keeps both the investigative and the vote-counting senses. Exact first date uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪进入法语，调查与点票两层含义都保留下来；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Scrutiny is recorded in English with the sense of a careful inquiry or examination.
items.cn: scrutiny 在十五世纪的英语文献中出现，意为谨慎的探究或检查。

items.en: The everyday phrase is under scrutiny, still one eye slowly passing over a surface to see what is hiding there.
items.cn: 现代英语最常用的说法是 under scrutiny，画面仍是一只眼睛缓缓扫过表面，看底下藏了什么。

note.en: Scrutiny belongs to the scrutin- family of searching and checking; its neighbours are inspection words and surveillance words that differ in who looks and how closely.
note.cn: scrutiny 属于表示「搜查」的 scrutin- 词族；它的邻居是各种检查、监督类词语，区别在于谁在看、看得有多细。

entries.definition: The verb for looking at something very carefully, built on the same scrutin- stem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「仔细检查、细看」，与 scrutiny 同根，只是词性不同。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same verb; the noun stays scrutiny in both spellings.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个动词的英式拼写；名词形式在英式与美式里都写作 scrutiny。

entries.definition: An old adjective meaning prying or given to searching inquiry; now rare.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，古义为「爱刨根问底的」，现已罕用。

entries.definition: A rare compound adjective describing something that escapes checking altogether.
entries.definitionCN: 复合形容词，意为「免于审查的」，用于形容完全躲过检查的事物。

entries.definition: A careful official look at a place or item to check its condition; more practical and on-site than scrutiny.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「检查、视察」，官方到现场查看状况，比 scrutiny 更偏实务。

entries.definition: A detailed study or test of something; broader than scrutiny and also used for medical and academic checks.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「检查、审查」，范围更广，也用于医学检查与考试。

entries.definition: Constant watching of a person or place, usually by police or cameras rather than by detailed reading.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「监视、监控」，多指警方或摄像头持续盯人，而非逐页细读。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root of rags and searching, and the phrases English actually keeps for close checking.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根「破布与翻找」，以及英语里表示仔细查看的常用搭配。

normal.en: scruta, the Latin for rags, gives scrutor, to search through, and so scrutiny, a careful search.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 scruta 是「破布」，由此生出 scrutor「翻找」与 scrutiny「细查」。

normal.en: Under scrutiny is the usual phrase, often with close or public in front of it.
normal.cn: under scrutiny 是最常见的说法，前面常加 close 或 public。

normal.en: Roman elections ended with a scrutinium, a slow one by one count of the ballots.
normal.cn: 古罗马选举结束时要做 scrutinium，即一张一张慢慢清点选票。

normal.en: The verb scrutinize keeps exactly the same stem, so check and checking share one word core.
normal.cn: 动词 scrutinize 词干完全相同，因此「检查」与「被检查」共用一个词核。

normal.en: Compare inspection: inspection checks whether a thing is in order, scrutiny asks whether it is honest.
normal.cn: 对比 inspection：inspection 查东西是否合规，scrutiny 更追问是否诚实。

abstract.en: Picture a hand turning over rags in a market heap until one small coin appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在市场旧货堆里翻动破布，直到一枚小硬币露出来。

abstract.en: Think of a torch beam moving slowly along a wall instead of sweeping the room at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一束手电光沿着墙面慢慢移动，而不是一下扫过整间屋子。

abstract.en: Imagine a spotlight on a stage: whoever stands under it cannot hide a torn cuff.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上的聚光灯：站在灯下的人藏不住一截破袖口。

examples.en: The spending of the charity has come under scrutiny from donors.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构的开支已受到捐助者的审查。

examples.en: Few details of the plan survived close scrutiny.
examples.cn: 这份计划经不起仔细推敲，几乎没有什么细节站得住。

examples.en: Editors give every headline careful scrutiny before it goes online.
examples.cn: 每条标题上网前，编辑都会仔细审核一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死窟俚您」——钻进死胡同的窟窿里也要盯个仔细，于是审查看得极细；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 scruta（破布、杂碎旧货）→ scrutor（翻找、搜查）→ scrutinium（搜查；清点选票）→ 古法语 scrutine → 英语 scrutiny，核心义「翻找藏起之物式的细查」。

sensesIntro.en: Scrutiny starts as a close, critical look at a thing, then widens into official investigation and public attention, and finally becomes a test that ideas must pass.
sensesIntro.cn: scrutiny 从对某个东西仔细审视开始，扩大到官方调查与公众关注，最后成为一种观点必须经受的检验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turning rags over in a heap, hunting for the one hidden thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在垃圾堆里翻动破布，搜寻那件被藏起来的东西。

branches.en: A close look at a document or object keeps the original hunting eye.
branches.cn: 对文件或物品的细看保留了最初那种搜寻的目光。

branches.en: Once an authority does the searching, the look becomes an investigation.
branches.cn: 当翻查的人换成权力机构，细看就变成调查。

branches.en: Many eyes replace one, and publicity turns the search into public attention.
branches.cn: 许多眼睛取代了一双眼睛，曝光让搜寻变成公众关注。

branches.en: Both ask whether something is true; one turns over paper, the other turns over arguments.
branches.cn: 两者都在追问真伪：一个翻纸页，一个翻论证。

branches.en: Official checks and public interest often arrive together in news reporting.
branches.cn: 新闻报道里，官方审查与公众关注往往一起出现。

intro.en: Scrutiny has no separable English prefix or suffix; the Latin stem scrutin- carries the whole search, and English builds the verb beside it.
intro.cn: scrutiny 在英语里没有可拆分的前缀或后缀，整个「搜查」意味都在拉丁词干 scrutin- 里，英语在它旁边造出了动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin scruta, scrutor and scrutinium are all recorded; the step from rags to searching is a matter of interpretation, not invention.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scruta、scrutor 与 scrutinium 均有文献记录；从「破布」到「搜查」的过渡属于解释层面，并非虚构。

items.example: Scruta names the heap that is searched through.
items.exampleCN: scruta 指的是被翻找的那堆东西。

items.example: Scrutor is a physical searching of a pile.
items.exampleCN: scrutor 是对一堆东西的实体翻找。

items.meaning: a search, inquiry; the counting of votes
items.example: Scrutinium adds the formal counting of votes.
items.exampleCN: scrutinium 增加了正式清点选票的含义。

items.example: Scrutiny keeps the noun sense unchanged.
items.exampleCN: scrutiny 完整保留了名词含义。

items.example: It forms scrutinize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 scrutinize。

items.example: It forms scrutinizer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 scrutinizer。

items.example: It ends the noun scrutiny.
items.exampleCN: 名词 scrutiny 以 -y 收尾。

items.example: It forms the rare scrutinous.
items.exampleCN: 它构成罕用的 scrutinous。

definition_zh: 扭打；混战；拖着脚蹭行；匆匆地扒弄
definition_en: a short, untidy fight, or to move or search while scraping and rustling things about
core_image: 两伙人在人群里推搡揪扯，鞋底在地面摩擦出沙沙声，又很快被拉开
scene: 散场时人群挤在出口，两名球迷突然互相推搡起来。A brief scuffle broke out near the ticket gate.
sceneCN: 这里 scuffle 是「短暂的扭打」（第 1 个义项：一阵混乱推搡的小打斗）；句意是售票闸口附近爆发了一场短暂的扭打。注意它强调时间短、动作乱、声音响，而不是有组织的战斗。

pos.zh: 名词：扭打；混战；短暂的打斗
动词：扭打；推搡厮打；拖着脚走；匆匆地扒弄

collocations.zh: 忽然打了起来；爆发扭打

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「参加扭打的人；拖脚走路者」
与本词同源、形近，义为「磨损；拖着脚走」（拖脚义部分词源与 scuffle 有交叉）
与本词同源，词根都来自「甩、掀动」义，义为「拖着脚走；洗牌」

senses.title: A short confused fight
senses.definition: a brief fight or struggle with pushing and grabbing rather than real fighting, often over quickly
senses.definitionCN: 时间短的推搡揪扯，多人乱作一团，谈不上真正的战斗，通常很快结束
senses.example: A scuffle started when someone grabbed the bag and ran.
senses.exampleCN: 有人抢了包就跑，于是一场扭打爆发了。
senses.why: The word is probably built on the root that gives shuffle, so the fight carries the noise of feet dragging and stumbling rather than the clash of weapons.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能来自与 shuffle「拖着走」同源的词根，所以这种打斗伴随的是鞋底拖拽踉跄的声音，而不是兵器相击。

senses.title: To struggle in a scrum
senses.definition: to fight or struggle briefly with someone in a confused, pushing way
senses.definitionCN: 与某人短暂地推搡厮打，动作混乱无序
senses.example: Two fans scuffled with security staff at the turnstile.
senses.exampleCN: 两名球迷在闸机口与安保人员推搡起来。
senses.why: The verb is the noun turned into motion: bodies shove against each other, and the scuffing noise follows each shove.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词变成了动作：身体互相顶撞，每一次推搡都伴着擦地的沙沙声。

senses.title: To drag the feet along
senses.definition: to move along slowly with the shoe soles scraping or rasping against the ground, as in a lazy or reluctant walk
senses.definitionCN: 鞋底蹭擦地面地缓慢移动，常见于懒散或不情愿的走路
senses.example: The children scuffled along the hall in their slippers.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们拖拉着拖鞋，沿着走廊蹭着走。
senses.why: The scraping noise that fills a short fight is first of all a noise of feet on the ground, so scuffle can name the dragging walk itself, not only the struggle.
senses.whyCN: 短促打斗里满是摩擦声，而这种声音本来就是鞋底蹭地的声音，因此 scuffle 也能直接指拖蹭着的走路，而不只是打斗。

senses.title: To rustle hurriedly through things
senses.titleCN: 匆匆翻动；沙沙作响地扒弄
senses.definition: to push and scrape things about quickly with the hands, often while searching or hurrying, making a rustling noise
senses.definitionCN: 双手快速推扒物品，常是急着翻找，并伴沙沙的声响
senses.example: She scuffled through the leaves to find her dropped keys.
senses.exampleCN: 她扒拉着落叶，找她掉落的钥匙。
senses.why: The same rough, busy contact with the ground is transferred to hands and objects, so scuffle ends up meaning any hurried, noisy fumbling.
senses.whyCN: 与地面接触时那种粗糙忙乱的感觉被转移到手上和物件上，于是 scuffle 泛指任何匆忙而带响的扒弄。

intro.en: Scuffle is uncertain in detail: it belongs to a family of English words built on a root meaning to shuffle or shove, and the first records are sixteenth-century.
intro.cn: scuffle 的细节来源不确定：它属于一个以「拖拽、推挤」为词根的英语词族，最早的文献记录在十六世纪。

items.en: The word is generally traced to a Germanic root seen in Dutch and Low German shove words, but the exact donor and form are source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为它可追到荷兰语与低地德语中表示「推、甩」的词，但具体来源语种与词形属于来源不确定。

items.en: Scuffle is first recorded in the sixteenth century as a verb and noun for a rushing, dragging movement or a scrappy fight.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语文献首先记录它作动词与名词，指慌乱的拖拽动作或零乱的扭打。

items.en: The sense of a confused, noisy scrap between people settles, and the word becomes common in reports of street trouble.
items.cn: 人与人之间混乱吵闹的小打斗这一义项稳定下来，此词常见于街头纠纷的记述。

items.en: Scuffle survives mainly in news reporting, where a brief scuffle at a gate or a protest is described in one calm line.
items.cn: 现代英语里 scuffle 主要出现在新闻报道中，用平静的一句描述闸口或抗议现场的短暂扭打。

items.en: American English keeps a separate usage for farmers scuffling the soil to clear weeds between crops; this sense has its own history.
items.cn: 美式英语保留了农业用法，指农人拖着工具松土除草；这一义项另有渊源。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same dragging and shuffling family; the near-meaning group gathers fight words that differ in size, noise and length.
note.cn: 形近组收「拖拽、蹭擦」同源的词；近义组收各种打斗词，区别在于规模、声响与持续时间。

entries.definition: To drag the feet or move things around in a lazy, untidy way; the closest relative of scuffle.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拖着脚走、把东西挪来挪去」，是 scuffle 最近的同源词。

entries.definition: To scrape or wear a surface, or to drag the feet; its dragging sense overlaps with scuffle.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「磨损、蹭」，也有拖脚义，与 scuffle 的拖脚义部分重叠。

entries.definition: To run with short quick steps; merely close in sound, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「小步快跑」；只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A person who scuffles; built directly from scuffle with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「扭打的人；拖脚走路的人」，由本词加表示「人」的后缀直接构成。

entries.definition: A large, noisy and violent fight, usually involving many people; bigger than a scuffle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喧闹的斗殴」，通常人数多、规模大，比 scuffle 严重。

entries.definition: A short struggle in which people push and pull at each other; very close, but often also used figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「扭打、角逐」，与 scuffle 极近，但更常用于比喻性争夺。

entries.definition: A noisy disturbance or quarrel; formal and usually reported in newspapers rather than in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喧闹的争吵、骚动」，语气正式，多见于新闻报道。

normalIntro.en: These hooks rely on the real sound picture of feet dragging on the ground and on the family the word belongs to.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子依赖「鞋底拖地」这一真实声音画面，以及这个词所属的同源词族。

normal.en: Shuffle and scuffle share a dragging root: shuffle is a lazy walk, scuffle is a noisy grab.
normal.cn: shuffle 与 scuffle 共享「拖拽」词根：shuffle 是懒散的走，scuffle 是吵闹的抓扯。

normal.en: A scuffle breaks out, then it is over in a minute: break out is the usual verb.
normal.cn: scuffle 常用 break out 搭配，意思是它突然爆发，一分钟内就结束。

normal.en: News reports keep it calm and short: a brief scuffle near the gate.
normal.cn: 新闻里它被写得平静而简短，比如闸口附近的短暂扭打。

normal.en: The sc- start is shared with scuff, scrape and scratch, all sounds of rough contact.
normal.cn: sc- 开头与 scuff、scrape、scratch 相同，都是粗糙摩擦的声音。

normal.en: Compare brawl: a brawl has many people and lasts, a scuffle has two or three and ends fast.
normal.cn: 对比 brawl：brawl 人多且持续，scuffle 两三人，很快结束。

abstract.en: Listen to two pairs of sneakers rubbing gravel at once and picture that noise becoming a shove.
abstract.cn: 想象两双球鞋同时蹭过碎石的声音，然后这声音变成了一次推搡。

abstract.en: See a doorway jammed for a second by two bodies pushing in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象门框被两个身体反向顶着，堵住了短短一秒。

abstract.en: Imagine leaves and dust kicked up under slow feet on a stone path.
abstract.cn: 想象石径上慢吞吞的脚把落叶和尘土蹭起。

examples.en: A scuffle broke out in the queue before the guards arrived.
examples.cn: 保安赶到之前，队伍里爆发了一场扭打。

examples.en: The two men scuffled briefly on the pavement.
examples.cn: 两个男人在人行道上短暂地扭打了一阵。

examples.en: Her purse fell in the scuffle and nobody noticed.
examples.cn: 扭打中她的手包掉了，却没有人注意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死卡夫」——两个人死死卡住对方的衣服推来推去，卡到衣服都磨破了，那就是扭打；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源于日耳曼语系中表示「推、甩」的词根（与 shuffle 同族），十六世纪进入英语；核心义「拖蹭着推挤」，由走路时鞋底擦地的声音扩展到人与人之间的零星扭打。

sensesIntro.en: Scuffle moves from a short pushing fight, to the act of struggling, to the scraping walk that shares its sound, and finally to hands that hurry noisily through things.
sensesIntro.cn: scuffle 从短暂的推搡打斗，到打斗这个动作本身，再到与它同一声响的拖脚蹭行，最后延伸到双手匆匆扒弄物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shoe soles rasping on the ground while two people shove and grab.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人推搡抓扯时，鞋底在地面上蹭擦出声。

branches.en: The dragging sound is attached to the event, so the fight itself is a scuffle.
branches.cn: 拖蹭的声音附着到事件上，这场打斗本身就被称作 scuffle。

branches.en: The event becomes an action: people scuffle while the noise continues.
branches.cn: 事件变成动作：人们推搡厮打，声响持续不断。

branches.en: The scraping noise survives on its own: an everyday walk with the soles rasping forward.
branches.cn: 蹭擦的声响独立保留下来：鞋底一路拖擦的日常走路。

branches.en: Both are short and noisy, and both are usually described as breaking out suddenly.
branches.cn: 两者都短促吵闹，通常都用突然爆发来描述。

branches.en: The rough noise of feet on the ground becomes the noise of hurrying hands.
branches.cn: 脚在地面上的粗糙声响，延伸到匆忙扒弄的双手。

intro.en: Scuffle has no clear English prefix or suffix; its final -le matches the ending of shuffle and other words of movement, and the sc- opening imitates rough contact.
intro.cn: scuffle 没有清晰的英语前后缀；词尾 -le 与 shuffle 等动作词相同，开头 sc- 模拟粗糙摩擦的声音。

latinIntro.en: Scuffle has no confirmed Latin ancestor, so the Latin list holds one word otherwise unconnected with it, and its root is treated as uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: scuffle 没有确证的拉丁语祖词，因此拉丁语条目只收一个与它并无亲缘关系的词，其词根按「来源不确定」处理。

items.meaningCN: 粗糙接触、摩擦的拟声词首
items.example: The sc- start also opens scrape and scratch.
items.exampleCN: sc- 开头也出现在 scrape 与 scratch 里。

items.example: The ending matches shuffle and wriggle.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾与 shuffle、wriggle 相同。

items.example: Shuffle shares the dragging root.
items.exampleCN: shuffle 共享「拖拽」词根。

items.example: Scuff is the shortest contact word in the family.
items.exampleCN: scuff 是词族里最短的接触类词。

items.example: Scuffle is the noun of the event.
items.exampleCN: scuffle 是这个事件的名词。

items.example: It forms scuffler.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 scuffler。

items.meaningCN: 扭打的人；拖脚走路的人
items.example: Scuffler names the person, not the noise.
items.exampleCN: scuffler 指人，而不是声音。

items.example: The verb takes -ed and -ing normally.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词照常加 -ed 与 -ing。

definition_zh: 海鸥；一只常见的海鸟，也指码头附近讨食的灰白鸟
definition_en: a common grey and white bird with long wings that lives near the sea and is often seen around harbours, beaches and city rubbish tips
core_image: 一只灰白的鸟停在码头的木桩上，盯着刚捞上来的鱼，翅膀上还带着海水的亮光
scene: 渔夫刚把一筐小鱼倒在甲板上，头顶立刻响起一片尖利的叫声。A seagull swooped down and snatched a fish from the basket.
sceneCN: 这里 seagull 是「海鸥」这一最直接的义项（第 1 个义项：常见的灰白色海鸟）；句意是一只海鸥俯冲下来，从筐里叼走了一条鱼。注意 seagull 是一个完整的复合词，不能拆成两个词使用。

pos.zh: 名词：海鸥；海边或港口的灰白色海鸟

derivatives.zh: seagull 的核心部分，鸟类学中泛指「鸥」，义为「海鸥一类的水鸟」
与 seagull 中的 gull 只是拼写相同、词源不同，义为「哄骗；蒙骗」
由 sea 与 fowl 复合构成，义为「海鸟」，与 seagull 同属构词法而非派生

senses.title: The bird itself
senses.definition: a grey and white bird, usually one of the large gulls such as the herring gull, commonly found near the sea
senses.definitionCN: 灰白相间的水鸟，通常指银鸥一类的大鸥，常见于海边
senses.example: Seagulls wheeled above the harbour all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 整个上午海鸥都在港口上空盘旋。
senses.why: Sea names the place and gull names the bird, so the compound simply says the gull that belongs to the sea.
senses.whyCN: sea 说明地方，gull 说明是哪种鸟，这个复合词直白地说出「属于海的鸥」。

senses.title: One of those birds nearby
senses.definition: used as a countable label for one individual bird of this kind, as in a seagull, two seagulls
senses.definitionCN: 作为可数名词称呼一只具体的海鸥，如 a seagull、two seagulls
senses.example: A seagull with a broken wing was resting on the pier.
senses.exampleCN: 一只折断翅膀的海鸥停在码头上休息。
senses.why: English needs a countable label for one bird, so the general word is used with a number or an article to count individuals.
senses.whyCN: 英语需要一个能数个体的称呼，于是这个总称加上冠词或数字，就用来数一只只的鸟。

senses.title: The scavenger of the quayside
senses.definition: the bird seen as an urban scavenger that raids rubbish bins, snatches food and crowds harbours and seaside cafés
senses.definitionCN: 被看作城市清道夫的鸟：翻垃圾箱、抢食物、挤满港口与海边小馆
senses.example: Seagulls swarmed the café tables as soon as the plates were cleared.
senses.exampleCN: 盘子刚收走，海鸥就蜂拥到小馆的桌上。
senses.why: Where people leave food, these birds find it, so the name carries a second, half comic picture of a cheeky opportunist.
senses.whyCN: 人一走开就留下食物，鸟自然找上门来，于是这个词带上第二个略带戏谑的形象：机灵碰运气的食客。

senses.title: The sound of the coast
senses.definition: the harsh mewing call that people hear on a coast and think of as a mark of seaside life
senses.definitionCN: 海岸上常听到的尖锐叫声，人们把它当作海边生活的标志
senses.example: The cry of a seagull drifted over the empty beach at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时分，海鸥的叫声飘过空荡的海滩。
senses.why: A bird that is heard before it is seen becomes a sound, so the cry itself is often named with the bird.
senses.whyCN: 先听见、后看见的鸟会变成一种声音，所以它的叫声也常被用这个词来命名。

intro.en: Seagull is a plain English compound of sea and gull, and gull itself is a bird name whose deeper origin is still debated.
intro.cn: seagull 是 sea 与 gull 的普通英语复合词，而 gull 本身是一个来源仍存争议的鸟名。

items.en: The English bird name gull is generally linked to Welsh and Cornish gwylan, a sea bird; whether the English word was borrowed or shares older ancestry is source uncertain.
items.cn: 英语中的鸟名 gull 一般认为与威尔士语、康沃尔语的 gwylan「海鸟」有关；英语是借入还是同源，属于来源不确定。

items.en: The first part, sea, is an old Germanic word recorded in Old English as sae and also carried in from Norse, with the same meaning.
items.cn: 前半部分 sea 是古老的日耳曼语词，古英语写作 sae，北欧语也带来同形同义的词。

items.en: The compound seagull is recorded from about the sixteenth century, when writers began to pair the bird name with the place it lives.
items.cn: seagull 这一复合形式约在十六世纪有记录，写作者开始把鸟名与它生活的场所配在一起。

items.en: Sea gull and seagull are both written; the closed form seagull is now the common everyday spelling, and it covers all large gulls near people.
items.cn: seagull 有分写与连写两种形式，现代日常写作多用连写的 seagull，泛指靠近人类的各种大鸥。

items.en: Americans often say just gull, especially in birding writing, while seagull stays the everyday word on British coasts.
items.cn: 美国人在观鸟文字里常只说 gull，而英国海边日常仍多用 seagull。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the parts of the compound and the bird names closest to it; the near-meaning group gathers other coast birds and birds of prey that share its shoreline.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词的组成部分与最接近的鸟名；近义组收其他海岸鸟类与同处一片海滩的猛禽。

entries.definition: The bird itself, without the sea: in birding, gull is the standard term for the whole family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，去掉 sea 之后单指「鸥」，观鸟文字中它是整个鸥科的标准称呼。

entries.definition: The throat or oesophagus; it merely begins with the same letters as gull, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咽喉、食道」；只是开头字母与 gull 相同，词源不同。

entries.definition: The first part of the compound; it shows the habitat that separates this bird from inland gulls.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词的前半部分，指明栖息地，也是把它与内陆的鸥区分开的地方。

entries.definition: Another sea compound built the same way; the pattern sea plus a noun is very productive.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个用 sea- 构成的复合词，可见「海洋语素 + 名词」这种构词法十分能产。

entries.definition: A big coastal water bird with a pouch under its bill; larger and heavier than a gull.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鹈鹕」，喙下有皮囊的大型海岸水鸟，比海鸥更大更重。

entries.definition: A dark diving bird seen on rocky coasts; unlike the gull, it catches fish under water.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鸬鹚」，常见的深色潜水鸟，与海鸥不同，它是在水下捕鱼的。

entries.definition: A slender sea bird related to gulls, with pointed wings and a quick diving flight.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「燕鸥」，与海鸥近缘的海鸟，翅膀尖细，俯冲迅捷。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real structure of the compound and the coast scenes where the bird actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用复合词的真实结构，以及海鸥真正出现的海边场景。

normal.en: Seagull is sea plus gull: one word says both the place and the bird.
normal.cn: seagull 就是 sea 加 gull：一个词同时说出地点和鸟。

normal.en: The plural is seagulls, and a group of them is a flock of seagulls.
normal.cn: 复数是 seagulls，一群海鸥说 a flock of seagulls。

normal.en: Birders usually just say gull, so the shorter word is the scientific one.
normal.cn: 观鸟者通常只说 gull，更简短的这个词反而更专业。

normal.en: The verb to gull means to fool, with a different history, so do not mix the two.
normal.cn: 动词 gull 表示欺骗，历史完全不同，别把两者混在一起。

normal.en: A seagull is not a unique species: it is a broad label for large gulls near people.
normal.cn: seagull 不是某个物种的专名，而是对各种靠近人类的大鸥的统称。

abstract.en: See a white bird with grey wings cut across the blue sky and then land on a wooden post.
abstract.cn: 想象一只白身灰翅的鸟划过蓝天，然后停在木桩上。

abstract.en: Hear a flat, harsh cry just above your head before you see the bird.
abstract.cn: 先听见头顶一声扁平刺耳的尖叫，然后才看见那只鸟。

abstract.en: Imagine a row of gulls waiting on a railing as if the café were theirs.
abstract.cn: 想象一排海鸥守在栏杆上，仿佛这家小馆是它们开的。

examples.en: A seagull perched on the harbour wall and watched the fishing boats.
examples.cn: 一只海鸥停在港口的石墙上，看着渔船。

examples.en: Seagulls followed the ferry across the bay.
examples.cn: 海鸥跟着渡轮飞过海湾。

examples.en: We threw the last of the bread to the seagulls on the beach.
examples.cn: 我们把最后一点面包扔给了沙滩上的海鸥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西鸥」——在西边的海上绕着飞的就是鸥，sea 是海，gull 是鸥；这只是谐音联想，与词源关系不大。

root: 英语 sea（海，古英语 sae）＋ gull（鸥，一般认为与威尔士语 gwylan「海鸟」有关，来源不确定）→ 十六世纪前后合为 seagull，字面义「海之鸥」。

sensesIntro.en: Seagull names the bird in general, then one countable bird, then that bird as a harbour scavenger, and finally the cry that sets the seaside soundscape.
sensesIntro.cn: seagull 先泛指这种鸟，再指一只只可数的个体，然后指在港口捡食的讨食鸟，最后指代表海边气息的鸣叫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey and white bird standing on a post above the water, eyeing the catch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只灰白的鸟立在水面上方的木桩上，盯着刚捞上来的鱼。

branches.en: The compound is a plain label, so it names the species group as a whole.
branches.cn: 这个复合词就是一张直白的标签，因此指整个鸥类。

branches.en: With an article or a number it counts one bird at a time.
branches.cn: 加上冠词或数字，它就能一只一只地数个体。

branches.en: Where people leave food, the bird appears, and becomes a harbour scavenger.
branches.cn: 人留下食物的地方就有它，于是它成了港口里的捡食者。

branches.en: The bird is known by its cry as much as its shape, so the name covers both.
branches.cn: 人们既凭外形也凭叫声认识它，于是这个词同时覆盖两者。

branches.en: Counting birds and telling scavenging stories both treat the gull as an individual character.
branches.cn: 数个体与讲捡食的故事，都把海鸥当作一个个有个性的角色。

intro.en: Seagull has no Latin prefixes or suffixes; it is a straightforward English compound, and the two parts keep their own meanings.
intro.cn: seagull 没有拉丁前缀或后缀，它是直白的英语复合词，两个部分各自保留本义。

latinIntro.en: Neither part comes from Latin, so no confirmed Latin relatives exist for seagull.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不是来自拉丁语，因此 seagull 没有确证的拉丁语同族词。

items.example: Sea names where the bird lives.
items.exampleCN: sea 指明这种鸟生活的地方。

items.meaning: a gull, a large grey and white sea bird
items.example: Gull alone is the birding term.
items.exampleCN: 单说 gull 就是观鸟用语中的「鸥」。

items.meaning: a gull living near the sea
items.example: Seagull joins the two parts into one word.
items.exampleCN: seagull 把两个部分合成一个词。

items.example: It yields seagulls.
items.exampleCN: 它构成复数 seagulls。

items.example: Sea- also begins seawall and seabird.
items.exampleCN: sea- 也出现在 seawall 与 seabird 开头。

items.meaning: any bird that lives on the sea
items.example: Seabird is the wider category above seagull.
items.exampleCN: seabird 是比 seagull 更宽的类别。

items.meaning: a sea bird, usually eaten or hunted
items.meaningCN: 海鸟，多指可供食用或捕猎的
items.example: Seafowl is an older word than seagull.
items.exampleCN: seafowl 是比 seagull 更古老的词。

items.example: Seaside names the place where tourists meet seagulls.
items.exampleCN: seaside 指游客遇到海鸥的海边地方。

definition_zh: 接缝；缝线；煤层；裂缝；（面部或情感上的）纹路、裂痕
definition_en: the line where two pieces of cloth, metal or rock are joined, or a thin line left by the joining
core_image: 两块布边对边压在一起，一针一针穿过去，留下一条细细的缝合线
scene: 矿工举着灯，指着岩壁上那条沿走向延伸的黑色细带。A thin seam of coal ran through the rock like a dark thread.
sceneCN: 这里 seam 是「矿层、煤层」（第 3 个义项：岩层中呈薄带状的一层矿藏）；句意：一条细细的煤层像深色的线一样穿过岩石。图中可辨识物件：矿灯、岩壁、细长矿层。

pos.zh: 缝合；把两块材料接合起来

collocations.zh: 胀得快要裂开；拥挤不堪
在接缝处散开；全面崩溃

derivatives.zh: 由 seam 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无缝的；衔接自然的」
由 seam 加 -y 构成，原指衣服翻出缝线的内里，引申为「阴暗的；丑恶的」
由 seam 加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，指「缝纫工；封边机」
由前缀 un- 加 seam 构成，义为「拆开缝线」

senses.title: The line where two pieces are sewn together
senses.definition: the line formed where two pieces of cloth or other material are joined by sewing
senses.definitionCN: 两块布或其他材料缝合处形成的那条线
senses.example: The seam of the sleeve had split open.
senses.exampleCN: 袖子的接缝裂开了。
senses.why: Old English seam first named the stitch work itself, so the joining line is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 seam 最初指缝的动作和针脚，所以「缝合处的那条线」是最古老的义项。

senses.title: The line joining metal or wood
senses.definition: the line along which two pieces of metal, wood or other hard material are welded or joined
senses.definitionCN: 两块金属、木料或其他硬质材料焊接或拼接处的线
senses.example: Welders checked the seam along the hull.
senses.exampleCN: 焊工检查了船体上的焊缝。
senses.why: The sewing line moved from cloth to hard materials, where welding now makes the same kind of joining line.
senses.whyCN: 缝合线从布料扩展到硬质材料，焊接在金属上做的是同一件事：把两块接成一条线。

senses.title: A thin layer of coal or ore
senses.definition: a thin layer of coal, mineral or rock lying between other layers of rock
senses.definitionCN: 夹在其他岩层之间的薄煤层或矿层
senses.example: Miners followed a narrow seam deep into the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工沿着一条窄窄的煤层深入山中。
senses.why: In the earth the joining line between rock layers shows up as a flat band, so miners borrowed seam for that band.
senses.whyCN: 在地层里，岩层之间的那条分界线呈现为一条扁平的带状层，矿工便借 seam 来指它。

senses.title: A crack or narrow opening
senses.definition: a long narrow crack or opening in a surface, such as a wall, a rock or the planks of a boat
senses.definitionCN: 墙面、岩石或船板等表面上细长狭窄的裂缝或开口
senses.example: Water seeped through a seam in the old planks.
senses.exampleCN: 水从旧船板的裂缝里渗了进来。
senses.why: A joined edge that fails opens into a gap, and the joining line turns into the line of a crack.
senses.whyCN: 原本接合的边缘一旦开裂就露出缝隙，接缝线随之变成裂缝线。

senses.title: A line on the face or in the skin
senses.definition: a line or ridge in the skin, or the scar line left by surgery or a wound
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上的纹路，或手术、伤口留下的疤痕线
senses.example: Deep seams marked the corners of his eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 他眼角有着深深的纹路。
senses.why: Skin drawn tight and folded leaves lines like stitches, and a stitched wound leaves a seam of its own.
senses.whyCN: 皮肤被拉紧、折叠就留下像针脚一样的线，缝合过的伤口也留下一条疤线。

senses.title: A hidden line of weakness
senses.definition: a point of weakness in a plan, an institution or a relationship where it may break
senses.definitionCN: 计划、机构或关系中可能破裂的薄弱处
senses.example: Cracks in the seam between the two allies were showing.
senses.exampleCN: 两个盟友之间的裂痕开始显现。
senses.why: Every joined thing has a line where it can part, so the word names any weak join in an argument or a friendship.
senses.whyCN: 任何接合起来的东西都有一条可能分开的线，于是这个词也用来指论点或关系中的薄弱接合处。

intro.en: Seam comes from Old English seam, a sewing, from the Germanic stem behind the verb that became English sew.
intro.cn: seam 来自古英语 seam（缝纫），源于与动词 sew（缝）同源的日耳曼语词干。

items.en: A reconstructed noun from the ancestor of the verb to sew, meaning a sewing or a stitch.
items.cn: 由「缝」这一动词的祖形构成的动词名词，重构义为「缝纫、针脚」。

items.en: Seam means a sewing, a stitch, or the line of stitches.
items.cn: 古英语 seam 指缝纫、一针针脚，或针脚形成的线。

items.en: Seam keeps the sewing sense and extends to the joined edge visible on cloth and leather.
items.cn: 中古英语 seam 保留缝纫义，并扩展到布、皮上可见的接合边。

items.en: Miners use seam for a thin layer of coal between other rock layers.
items.cn: 大约从十五世纪起，矿工用 seam 指夹在其他岩层之间的薄煤层。

items.en: Welding, surgery and figurative speech extend the word to metal, scar lines and weak points in plans.
items.cn: 现代英语经焊接、外科与比喻用法，把该词扩展到金属、疤痕线和计划的薄弱处。

note.en: Seam is a joining line: it looks like seam, seem and seam, and it sits near stitches, grooves and cracks.
note.cn: seam 是「接合的线」：它与 seem、seam 等形近词易混，也与「针脚、沟槽、裂缝」同一义场。

entries.definition: to appear to be
entries.definitionCN: 似乎；看起来（与 seam 同音但词源不同）

entries.definition: to scatter seed, from a root once shared with sewing
entries.definitionCN: 播种；其词源与「缝」的祖形有过联系

entries.definition: the line where something ends or meets another surface
entries.definitionCN: 边缘；界限（拼写不同，词源不同，只是概念相邻）

entries.definition: a single loop of thread made by a needle
entries.definitionCN: 一针缝线；针脚

entries.definition: a long narrow cut or channel in a surface
entries.definitionCN: 沟槽；凹槽

entries.definition: to join pieces of metal by heat
entries.definitionCN: 焊接；使熔化接合

entries.definition: a narrow break in a hard surface
entries.definitionCN: 裂缝；裂痕

normalIntro.en: Seam is the line of joining: wherever two things meet and are fixed together, a seam runs.
normalIntro.cn: seam 是「接合的线」：两样东西碰在一起、固定起来的地方，就有一条 seam。

normal.en: A seam is what a needle leaves when it joins two pieces.
normal.cn: 针把两块布接起来留下的那条线，就是 seam。

normal.en: Seam of coal names the thin band between rock layers.
normal.cn: seam of coal 指岩层之间的薄煤层。

normal.en: To burst at the seams means the stitches give way.
normal.cn: burst at the seams 意为接缝撑裂，引申为拥挤不堪。

normal.en: Seamless takes the -less suffix and means without a seam.
normal.cn: seamless 由后缀 -less 构成，意思是「无缝的」。

normal.en: Do not confuse seam with seem, which means to appear.
normal.cn: 别把 seam 和 seem 混淆，seem 意为「看起来」。

abstract.en: Picture a jacket turned inside out, its seams showing.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套里子朝外翻出来，接缝全都露在外面。

abstract.en: Imagine a welder running a bright bead of metal down two plates.
abstract.cn: 想象焊工把一条亮亮的焊缝拉过两块钢板。

abstract.en: Think of a thin black line running through a cliff face.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细细的黑线横穿整面岩壁。

examples.en: The tailor pressed the seams flat before sewing the lining.
examples.cn: 裁缝把接缝压平，然后才缝上衬里。

examples.en: Engineers inspected the welded seam for small holes.
examples.cn: 工程师检查焊缝有没有小孔。

examples.en: The warehouse was bursting at the seams.
examples.cn: 仓库已经胀得满满当当。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「细木」——缝线细得像木纹一样平直；这只是拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 seam（缝纫、针脚）→ 针脚形成的接合线 → 布料接缝、金属焊缝 → 地层薄层、裂缝与弱点。与动词 sew（缝）同源。

sensesIntro.en: Seam begins as the line left by stitching, moves to welds and then to the flat bands and cracks of rock, and ends with the lines written on skin and on plans.
sensesIntro.cn: seam 先是针脚留下的接合线，扩展到焊缝，再用于岩层中的薄层和裂缝，最后指写在皮肤上和计划里的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle pulling thread through two edges pressed together, leaving one even line.
core.cn: 核心意象：针线穿过两块对齐的布边，留下一条均匀的缝线。

branches.en: The visible line of stitches is the first sense.
branches.cn: 看得见的针脚线是第一个义项。

branches.en: Hard materials join by heat, so the line becomes a welded seam.
branches.cn: 硬材料靠高温接合，这条线就成了焊缝。

branches.en: Inside rock, a joining line shows as a flat thin band, which miners read as coal.
branches.cn: 在岩石里，接合线表现为扁平的薄带，矿工读作煤层。

branches.en: When the joined edges part, the seam turns into a crack.
branches.cn: 接合边一旦分开，接缝就变成裂缝。

branches.en: A seam is always both visible and fragile, which is why it serves for skin lines and for weak points in plans.
branches.cn: seam 既可见又脆弱，因此既能指皮肤上的线，也能指计划中的薄弱处。

intro.en: Seam is a Germanic noun from the sewing root, with English descendants such as seamless, seamy and seamer.
intro.cn: seam 是源自「缝」这一词干的日耳曼语名词，英语中衍生出 seamless、seamy、seamer 等词。

latinIntro.en: Seam is not a Latin word, so there is no Latin cognate; Latin suere, to sew, is a distant cousin rather than the source.
latinIntro.cn: seam 不是拉丁语词，没有拉丁同源词；拉丁语 suere（缝）只是远亲，并非来源。

items.meaning: the line where two pieces are joined
items.example: The seam ran neatly down the back.
items.exampleCN: 接缝整整齐齐地沿着背后一条线下去。

items.example: They seamed the panels before polishing.
items.exampleCN: 他们在打磨前先把几块拼板接合起来。

items.example: Rain soaked through the seams.
items.exampleCN: 雨水从接缝处渗了进来。

items.example: His seamed face showed years outdoors.
items.exampleCN: 他满是纹路的脸显出常年在户外的痕迹。

items.meaning: the act of joining by a seam
items.example: Seaming was done by hand.
items.exampleCN: 缝合这道工序是手工完成的。

items.example: The artist drew one seamless line.
items.exampleCN: 画家一笔画成了一条连贯的线。

items.example: The suffix -less forms seamless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 seamless。

items.example: The novel shows the seamy side of the city.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说写的是这座城市阴暗的一面。

items.example: The suffix -y forms seamy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 seamy。

items.example: She unseamed the old coat to reuse the wool.
items.exampleCN: 她把旧外套拆开，好把毛料再派用场。

definition_zh: 烧灼；烫焦；使枯萎；使变得冷酷；（记忆中）深深烙下
definition_en: to burn or scorch the surface of something, drying or hardening it
core_image: 一块烧红的铁按在皮肉上，表面立刻焦黄、收紧，边缘卷起
scene: 厨师把牛排按在烧得发红的铸铁锅上，屋里立刻充满油烟。The hot pan seared the meat in a few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 sear 是「高温煎封」（第 2 个义项：用极高的火力快速煎烤表面）；句意：滚烫的锅在几秒钟内就把肉煎封了。图中可辨识物件：铸铁锅、牛排、腾起的白烟。

pos.zh: 烧灼；烫焦；煎封；使枯萎；使冷酷

derivatives.zh: 由 sear 加 -ing 构成，义为「灼热的；猛烈的、刻骨铭心的」
与 sear 同一词源的形容词，义为「干枯的、枯萎的」
由 sear 加过去分词后缀构成，义为「表面焦硬的；被烙下印记的」

senses.title: To burn the surface of something
senses.definition: to burn the surface of something with intense heat so that it hardens or changes colour
senses.definitionCN: 用极高的温度烧灼某物的表面，使其变硬或变色
senses.example: The iron seared a dark mark into the board.
senses.exampleCN: 熨斗在板上烫出了一道深色痕迹。
senses.why: Old English sear meant dry, and fire takes moisture away, so searing is burning something until its surface dries.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 sear 本义为「干燥的」，火会带走水分，所以 sear 就是烧到表面变干脆。

senses.title: To fry a surface at very high heat
senses.definition: to cook the outside of meat or fish quickly in a very hot pan so that a brown crust forms
senses.definitionCN: 用滚烫的锅快速煎烤肉或鱼的表面，形成褐色硬壳
senses.example: Sear the chicken skin side down first.
senses.exampleCN: 先把鸡皮那一面朝下煎封。
senses.why: Cooking borrows the heat: a hot pan makes the same dry brown crust, and the word names the step.
senses.whyCN: 烹饪借用了这种高温：热锅造成同样的干褐色硬壳，于是这个词就成了这道工序的名字。

senses.title: To dry up plants
senses.definition: to dry up and wither plants or land through great heat
senses.definitionCN: 因酷热使植物或土地干枯、枯萎
senses.example: Frost seared the young leaves overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜霜冻把嫩叶都打蔫了。
senses.why: The old sense was simply dry, so sear also names what sun or frost does when it pulls all moisture away.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的旧义就是「干」，所以日照或霜冻把水分全部抽走时，也用 sear。

senses.title: To make someone cold and unfeeling
senses.definition: to harden a person so that their feelings become dry and unresponsive
senses.definitionCN: 使某人变得冷硬、不再有感情反应
senses.example: Years of loss had seared his sympathy.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的失去让他的同情心变得冷硬。
senses.why: Heat that hardens a surface becomes a metaphor for a person whose warm feelings have been dried out.
senses.whyCN: 把表面烤硬的高温被用作比喻，指一个人心里的温情被烤干、变硬了。

senses.title: To fix something in the memory
senses.definition: to fix a memory or an emotion so sharply that it cannot be forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 把记忆或情感印得极深，以至无法忘掉
senses.example: The image was seared into her mind.
senses.exampleCN: 那个画面深深烙进了她的脑海。
senses.why: A seared surface keeps its mark for good, so a seared memory is one that has been stamped in and will not fade.
senses.whyCN: 被烤过的表面会永远留下印记，所以被「seared」的记忆就是被烙进去、不会淡去的记忆。

intro.en: Sear comes from Old English sear, dry or withered, a Germanic adjective that also produced the modern adjective sere.
intro.cn: sear 来自古英语形容词 sear（干燥的、枯萎的），同源形容词在现代英语中写作 sere。

items.en: A reconstructed adjective meaning dry, from an older Indo-European root for drying up.
items.cn: 一般重构为一个表示「干燥」的形容词，可追溯到更早的表示「干涸」的印欧词根。

items.en: Sear is an adjective meaning dry, withered or sere.
items.cn: 古英语 sear 是形容词，意为「干燥的、枯萎的」。

items.en: The word is used as a verb: to dry up, to wither, to burn the surface.
items.cn: 中古英语中开始用作动词：使干、使枯萎、烧灼表面。

items.en: Searing enters cookery for the hot surface of grilled or roasted meat.
items.cn: 十六世纪前后，sear 进入烹饪用语，指把烤肉的表面烧成硬壳。

items.en: The dried-over surface becomes an image for hardness of feeling and for marks fixed in the mind.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，「表面被烤硬」被用作比喻，指感情的冷硬和烙在心里的印记。

note.en: Sear is heat acting on a surface: it looks like seer and sere, and it sits near scorch, singe and burn.
note.cn: sear 是「高温作用于表面」：它与 seer、sere 形近，又与 scorch、singe、burn 同一义场。

entries.definition: dry and withered
entries.definitionCN: 干枯的；枯萎的（与 sear 同源，是同源形容词）

entries.definition: a person who sees the future
entries.definitionCN: 预言者；先知（与 sear 同音但词源不同）

entries.definition: a line where two pieces are joined
entries.definitionCN: 接缝（拼写相近，但只是形近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to burn the surface lightly so that it changes colour
entries.definitionCN: 烤焦；烧焦表面

entries.definition: to burn the ends of hair or fur slightly
entries.definitionCN: 燎；轻微烧焦

entries.definition: to be on fire or to damage something with fire
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧；烧伤

entries.definition: to become dry and shrivelled
entries.definitionCN: 枯萎；凋谢

normalIntro.en: Sear is dryness made by heat: the surface goes dry, hard and brown at the touch of fire.
normalIntro.cn: sear 是「被热造成的干燥」：一碰到火，表面就变得又干、又硬、又黄。

normal.en: Searing heat means heat that dries and burns everything it touches.
normal.cn: searing heat 指一种触之即干、触之即焦的酷热。

normal.en: To sear the meat is to cook its outside hard and brown first.
normal.cn: sear the meat 就是先把肉的外层煎得又硬又黄。

normal.en: Be seared into the memory means fixed there as if burnt in.
normal.cn: be seared into the memory 意为像被烙进去一样牢牢记住。

normal.en: Sere is the same old adjective, now meaning dry and withered.
normal.cn: sere 是同一个古老形容词的另一种写法，意为「干枯的」。

normal.en: Compare scorch: scorch marks a surface, sear adds the idea of hardening it.
normal.cn: 对比 scorch：scorch 是烤焦表面，sear 还多一层「烤硬」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a red-hot brand pressed onto wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一块烧红的烙印压到木头上。

abstract.en: See the white edge where meat meets a hot pan.
abstract.cn: 看看肉片贴到热锅上时那一圈白色的边。

abstract.en: Imagine grass in late summer, stiff and brown.
abstract.cn: 想象夏末的草地，干硬发黄。

examples.en: She seared the fish in a very hot pan for one minute.
examples.cn: 她在滚烫的锅里把鱼煎封了一分钟。

examples.en: The searing heat kept everyone indoors.
examples.cn: 炙热逼得所有人都待在屋内。

examples.en: The day was seared into his memory.
examples.cn: 那一天深深刻在他的记忆里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西尔」——烤肉贴到铁板上「嗤」的一声冒烟烫焦；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 sear（干燥的、枯萎的）→ 中古英语动词「使干、烧灼表面」→ 现代英语 sear（烧焦、煎封、烙印）。同源形容词为 sere。

sensesIntro.en: Sear starts with fire drying out a surface, passes through cookery, then dries plants, hardens feelings and finally stamps memories in place.
sensesIntro.cn: sear 从火把表面烤干讲起，经由烹饪煎封，再到植物干枯、感情冷硬，最后落在把记忆烙进心里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red-hot surface touching skin or meat and leaving a dry, brown, hardened mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：烧红的表面碰到皮肤或肉，留下一块干硬发黄的印记。

branches.en: Fire dries and burns a surface, which is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 火把表面烤干烧焦，这是本义。

branches.en: A hot pan does the same to meat, so cooking takes the word.
branches.cn: 热锅对肉做同样的事，于是烹饪用上了这个词。

branches.en: Heat without fire, from sun or frost, dries plants and is called searing too.
branches.cn: 没有明火的高温，来自日照或霜冻，把植物烤干，也叫 sear。

branches.en: Hardened meat becomes hardened feelings, the first figurative step.
branches.cn: 肉变硬可以转成感情变硬，这是第一个比喻义。

branches.en: A burnt mark stays forever, so a seared memory is one that will not fade.
branches.cn: 烧过的印记会永久留下，所以被 seared 的记忆不会淡去。

intro.en: Sear is a Germanic word with little word-building: searing, seared and the adjective sere are its main English relatives.
intro.cn: sear 是日耳曼语词，构词不多，主要亲属是 searing、seared 与形容词 sere。

latinIntro.en: Sear has no Latin source; Latin torrere, to scorch, is the usual Latin verb for the same action but is a different word.
latinIntro.cn: sear 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 torrere（烤焦）虽表示同样的动作，却是另一个词。

items.example: The flame seared the paper edges.
items.exampleCN: 火焰把纸边烫焦了。

items.example: A hot iron sears the fabric fast.
items.exampleCN: 热熨斗很快就把布料烫焦。

items.example: The chef served seared tuna.
items.exampleCN: 厨师端上了煎封过的金枪鱼。

items.example: The searing heat lasted all week.
items.exampleCN: 那股炙热持续了整整一周。

items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms searing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 searing。

items.example: Sere leaves fell from the tree.
items.exampleCN: 枯黄的叶子从树上落下。

items.meaningCN: 构成过去分词或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms seared.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 seared。

items.meaning: the act of scorching a surface
items.example: Searing locks the juices inside the steak.
items.exampleCN: 煎封能把牛排骨汁锁住。

items.example: Older texts count the sear on the timber.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文献会提到木料上的焦痕。

definition_zh: 使隔离；使隐蔽；使独处；（主动）隐居；把某物藏在不被看到的地方
definition_en: to keep someone or something apart from other people or places, often so that it stays private
core_image: 一扇厚重的木门在身后关上，插上门闩，外面的一切声响都被挡在门另一边
scene: 作家拖着书稿走进山间小屋，把门关上，窗帘也拉了起来。She secluded herself in the cabin to finish the novel.
sceneCN: 这里 seclude 是「使独处、隐居」（第 3 个义项：自己主动与外界隔离）；句意：她把自己关在小屋里，好把小说写完。图中可辨识物件：山间小屋、厚窗帘、成叠书稿。

pos.zh: 僻静的；与外界隔绝的（以过去分词形式作形容词）

derivatives.zh: 由 seclude 加 -ed 构成，义为「僻静的；与外界隔绝的」
由 seclude 的拉丁语名词形 seclusio 而来，义为「隐居；隔离」
seclusion 加 -ive 构成，义为「喜欢独居的；有隐居倾向的」

senses.title: To keep someone apart from others
senses.definition: to keep a person away from other people, sometimes against their will
senses.definitionCN: 使某人远离其他人，有时是违背其意愿的
senses.example: Monks secluded the young novice in a separate cell.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们把年幼的见习修士隔离在一间单独的屋子里。
senses.why: The Latin prefix se- marks apart, so secluding is a closing off that sets a person apart from the group.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 se- 表示「分开」，所以 seclude 就是把人同群体隔开的一道封闭。

senses.title: To hide a place from view
senses.definition: to place a building, garden or object where it is mostly hidden and out of sight
senses.definitionCN: 把建筑、花园或物件安置在几乎看不见的地方
senses.example: Tall hedges seclude the house from the road.
senses.exampleCN: 高高的树篱把房子挡在马路视线之外。
senses.why: Closing something off also hides it, so a secluded place is one shut away behind trees, walls or distance.
senses.whyCN: 封闭也意味着隐藏，所以 secluded 的地方就是被树、墙或距离关在后面的地方。

senses.title: To withdraw into privacy
senses.definition: to go apart from other people on purpose, especially to work, rest or think
senses.definitionCN: 有意离开他人独处，尤指为了工作、休息或思考
senses.example: He secludes himself every morning to write.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天上午都闭门写作。
senses.why: When the person does the closing, the word turns from being shut away to choosing to shut oneself away.
senses.whyCN: 当关门的人是本人时，这个词就从「被隔离」变成「主动把自己关起来」。

senses.title: To keep something separate in study
senses.definition: to treat a single factor or group on its own, apart from the others being studied
senses.definitionCN: 在研究某一因素或群体时把它单独抽出，与其他对象分开处理
senses.example: The study secludes rural pupils from the urban sample.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把农村学生从城镇样本中单独抽出。
senses.why: Scientific wording reuses the closed-off image for data: one set is shut away from the rest so it can be shown alone.
senses.whyCN: 科研写法把「封闭」用到数据上：把一组同其他数据隔开，好单独呈现。

intro.en: Seclude comes from Latin secludere, made of se-, aside, and claudere, to shut.
intro.cn: seclude 来自拉丁语 secludere，由 se-（在旁边、分开）和 claudere（关闭）构成。

items.en: Claudere means to shut or to close a door, the root of close and exclude.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭、关门，是 close、exclude 等词的词根。

items.en: Se- here carries the idea of apart, so secludere means to shut something off or aside.
items.cn: 这里的 se- 带有「分开、在一边」的意思，secludere 即「把某物关到一边、隔开」。

items.en: Classical Latin uses secludere of shutting off a place or a person.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语已用 secludere 表示把地方或人隔开。

items.en: Seclude enters English meaning to shut off from access or from company.
items.cn: 约在十五至十六世纪，seclude 进入英语，意为「隔开、不让接近」。

items.en: Secluded becomes the common adjective for quiet hidden places; the reflective use with oneself develops after this.
items.cn: secluded 成为形容幽静隐蔽之处的常用形容词，其后又发展出与 oneself 连用的自反用法。

note.en: Seclude shares the Latin verb to shut: it looks like conclude, exclude and include, and it sits near isolate, withdraw and hide.
note.cn: seclude 与「关闭」这一拉丁语动词同根，与 conclude、exclude、include 形近，也与「隔离、退隐」同一义场。

entries.definition: to shut someone out and keep them from joining
entries.definitionCN: 把某人排除在外，不让他加入

entries.definition: to shut something to an end, so to finish or decide
entries.definitionCN: 把某事关上、使其结束，即得出结论

entries.definition: to shut something inside a group or container
entries.definitionCN: 把某物关在群体或容器之内，即包含

entries.definition: to put something quite alone, away from all others
entries.definitionCN: 使孤立；使完全分离

entries.definition: to pull back from a place or from other people
entries.definitionCN: 撤退；退出；隐退

entries.definition: to put something where it cannot be seen
entries.definitionCN: 藏起；遮蔽

entries.definition: to keep someone safe under cover
entries.definitionCN: 庇护；遮盖

normalIntro.en: Seclude is a Latin door closing apart: se- aside plus claudere to shut.
normalIntro.cn: seclude 是一道把人与外界隔开的拉丁语门：se-（在一边）加 claudere（关闭）。

normal.en: The root -clude appears in exclude, include and conclude.
normal.cn: 词根 -clude 出现在 exclude、include、conclude 里。

normal.en: To seclude oneself from the world is to shut oneself away.
normal.cn: seclude oneself from the world 就是与世隔绝。

normal.en: A secluded beach is a beach that is hidden and quiet.
normal.cn: a secluded beach 就是隐蔽又安静的海滩。

normal.en: Seclusion, the noun, names the state of being shut apart.
normal.cn: 名词 seclusion 指被隔开、幽居的状态。

normal.en: Compare isolate: isolate stresses being alone, seclude stresses a place closed off.
normal.cn: 对比 isolate：isolate 强调孤立，seclude 强调被封闭在某处。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy oak door closing with a soft thud.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇厚重的橡木门轻轻一响、合上了。

abstract.en: Think of a house hidden behind a wall of tall trees.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋藏在整排高树后面的房子。

abstract.en: See a writer pulling the curtains shut before starting work.
abstract.cn: 想象一位作家开始写作前把窗帘拉上。

examples.en: The family secluded the sick child for two weeks.
examples.cn: 这家人把生病的孩子隔离了两周。

examples.en: They own a secluded cottage by the lake.
examples.cn: 他们在湖边有一栋僻静的小屋。

examples.en: After the tour he secluded himself in his studio.
examples.cn: 巡演结束之后，他把自己关在工作室里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死克碌的」——把自己关在僻静小屋里埋头苦干，忙得与世隔绝；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 se-（分开、在一边）+ claudere（关闭）→ secludere（隔开）→ 英语 seclude（隔离、隐蔽）；同根词有 exclude、include、conclude、preclude。

sensesIntro.en: Seclude starts with a person shut away from others, extends to a place hidden from view, then to a deliberate withdrawal, and finally to a set singled out in research.
sensesIntro.cn: seclude 先从人被隔开讲起，再扩展到隐蔽的地方，然后是主动退隐，最后落在研究中被单列出来的一组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door closed behind you, so that the outside stays outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：门在身后关上，外面的世界留在外面。

branches.en: Shutting a person apart from others is the first sense.
branches.cn: 把人同他人隔开是第一个义项。

branches.en: A place shut off is a place out of sight, the hidden sense.
branches.cn: 被隔开的地方也是看不见的地方，这是隐蔽义。

branches.en: When the person does the closing, the word means chosen privacy.
branches.cn: 当关门的人是本人时，这个词就指主动选择的独处。

branches.en: Research borrows the same door: one group is shut away from the rest.
branches.cn: 科研借用同一扇门：把一组数据同其余数据隔开。

branches.en: A hidden place and a retreat both depend on one wall between a person and the crowd.
branches.cn: 隐蔽之所与退隐之所，都靠人和人群之间的那一堵墙。

intro.en: Seclude is built from the Latin prefix se- and the root -clude, to shut, seen in exclude, include and conclude.
intro.cn: seclude 由拉丁语前缀 se- 与词根 -clude（关闭）构成，同根词有 exclude、include、conclude。

latinIntro.en: Latin claudere means to shut, and se- means apart; secludere shuts something off.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 claudere 意为关闭，se- 意为分开，secludere 即把某物关到一边。

items.example: The prefix se- adds apartness to the root.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 se- 给词根加上「分开」的意思。

items.example: The root -clude appears in many English words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -clude 出现在许多英语单词里。

items.example: Claudere is the source of the root -clude.
items.exampleCN: claudere 是词根 -clude 的来源。

items.example: Walls seclude the courtyard from the street.
items.exampleCN: 围墙把庭院同街道隔开。

items.example: The rule excludes late entries.
items.exampleCN: 该规则不接受迟交的作品。

items.example: The price includes breakfast.
items.exampleCN: 价格包含早餐。

items.example: The talk concluded at noon.
items.exampleCN: 讲座在中午结束。

items.example: The injury precludes further play.
items.exampleCN: 这次受伤使他不能再上场了。

items.meaning: the state of being shut apart
items.example: She wrote most of the book in seclusion.
items.exampleCN: 这本书的大部分她是在隐居状态中写成的。

items.meaning: forming nouns of action or state
items.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或状态的名词
items.example: The suffix -ion forms seclusion.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 seclusion。

definition_zh: 隐居；与世隔绝；僻静（的地方）；不被打扰的状态
definition_en: the state of living alone or in a quiet private way, kept separate from other people
core_image: 一扇房门关上，把喧闹的人群留在门外
scene: 她在山间小屋住了一个夏天，只为求得一段清静。She spent a summer in a mountain cabin, seeking seclusion from a noisy world.
sceneCN: 这里 seclusion 是「隐居、与世隔绝」（第 1 个义项：离群索居的状态）；句意：她在山间小屋住了一个夏天，只为远离喧闹，求一份清静。

collocations.phrase: the seclusion of a quiet village

derivatives.zh: 动词原形，由名词回构而来，义为「使隔离；使隐退」
过去分词作形容词，义为「隐蔽的；僻静的」
加后缀 -ive，义为「好隐居的；喜欢独处的」

senses.title: Withdrawal from the company of others
senses.definition: the state of living apart from other people, often by choice
senses.definitionCN: 离开人群而独自生活，常出于自愿
senses.example: After retiring, the poet lived in seclusion for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 退休后，这位诗人在隐居中度过了十年。
senses.why: The Latin verb secludere means to shut off, and a person who is shut off from others lives in withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 secludere 意为「把……关在外面」，被关在人群之外的人，过的正是隐居生活。

senses.title: A quiet and private place
senses.definition: a place hidden from view or free from the disturbance of other people
senses.definitionCN: 不被人看见、不受他人打扰的地方
senses.example: We ate lunch in the seclusion of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在花园的僻静处吃了午饭。
senses.why: The abstract state of being closed off easily becomes the name of a place that provides it.
senses.whyCN: 「封闭起来」这种状态一具体化，就用来指能提供这种状态的地方。

senses.title: Freedom from disturbance
senses.definition: the condition of being undisturbed by other people, noise, or attention
senses.definitionCN: 不受他人、噪音或关注打扰的状态
senses.example: She wrote the novel in the seclusion of a country house.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一座乡间住宅的清静中写完了这部小说。
senses.why: Being set apart does not only mean loneliness, it also means being shielded from noise and attention.
senses.whyCN: 被隔开不一定是孤独，也意味着被挡在噪音与关注之外，于是衍生出「清静」。

senses.title: The act of shutting something off
senses.definition: the act of separating a person or thing from others, as in medical or official practice
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物与他人分开的行为，见于医疗或官方做法
senses.example: The patient asked for seclusion during treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗期间病人要求隔离护理。
senses.why: This sense is the verb acted out, the closing of a door between one person and everyone else.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是动词动作本身，就是在一人与众人之间把门关上。

senses.title: A secluded retreat
senses.definition: a dwelling or lodging set far from crowds and everyday traffic
senses.definitionCN: 远离人群与日常喧嚣的居所
senses.example: His seclusion by the lake became a famous refuge.
senses.exampleCN: 他在湖畔的幽居后来成了有名的避风港。
senses.why: When people speak of someone in seclusion, they often mean the retreat itself, the building or spot that keeps the world out.
senses.whyCN: 说起某人的隐居时，常指那座隐居住所，即把外界挡在门外的那处地方。

intro.en: Seclusion comes from Latin secludere, to shut off, made of se-, apart, and claudere, to close. It reached English through the noun seclusio.
intro.cn: seclusion 来自拉丁语 secludere（关在外面），由 se-（分开）与 claudere（关闭）构成，经名词 seclusio 进入英语。

items.en: Claudere means to close or shut, and se- marks separation.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭，se- 表示分开。

items.en: Secludere means to shut off or separate a person or place from others.
items.cn: secludere 意为把人或地方与他人隔开关闭。

items.en: Seclusio is the abstract noun, a shutting off.
items.cn: seclusio 是对应的抽象名词，意为「隔开」。

items.en: Seclusion enters English as a formal noun for retirement from the world.
items.cn: seclusion 在十七世纪进入英语，作为正式名词表示退隐。

items.en: The word broadens to mean any quiet place or freedom from disturbance.
items.cn: 现代英语中词义扩展，指任何清静之处或不受打扰的状态。

items.en: The verb seclude and the adjective secluded are re-formed around the noun.
items.cn: 围绕这个名词又回构出动词 seclude 与形容词 secluded。

note.en: Seclusion shares the Latin claudere closing root with closets and clauses, and sits near words for solitude, isolation, and privacy.
note.cn: seclusion 与 closets、clauses 共享拉丁关闭词根 claudere，语义上也挨着独处、隔离、私密这一群词。

entries.definitionCN: 使隔离；使隐退

entries.definition: hidden away from other people
entries.definitionCN: 隐蔽的；僻静的

entries.definition: fond of staying apart from others

entries.definition: the state of being alone
entries.definitionCN: 独处；孤独

entries.definition: separation from others, often forced

entries.definition: the state of being free from public attention

normalIntro.en: Seclusion is the noun of a door shut on the crowd, built from se- apart and claudere to close.
normalIntro.cn: seclusion 是「对人群关门」的名词，由 se-（分开）与 claudere（关闭）构成。

normal.en: In seclusion is the fixed phrase for living out of public view.
normal.cn: in seclusion 是表示隐居、闭门不出的固定搭配。

normal.en: Seek seclusion means to look for a quiet place away from people.
normal.cn: seek seclusion 表示寻找远离人群的清静。

normal.en: Thousands of monks chose seclusion in the mountains for a lifetime of study.
normal.cn: 许多僧人选择山中隐居，终身研习。

normal.en: A secluded house is the adjective form of the same root, meaning private and hard to find.
normal.cn: secluded house 用的是同一词根的形容词，表示私密而难寻。

normal.en: Compare solitude, which stresses being alone, with seclusion, which stresses being shut off.
normal.cn: 对比 solitude 强调独自一人，seclusion 强调被隔开关闭。

abstract.en: Picture a cottage behind a high hedge, its gate latched from inside, the noise of the village far away.
abstract.cn: 想象一座藏在高树篱后面的小屋，门闩从里面插上，村庄的喧闹远在门外。

abstract.en: Imagine finding a bench in the deepest corner of a garden, where nobody walks past.
abstract.cn: 想象在花园最深的角落找到一张长凳，没有人从那里经过。

abstract.en: Think of a library study room with a sealed door, where no sound can get in.
abstract.cn: 想象图书馆里一间密闭的自习室，什么声音都进不来。

examples.en: The novelist spent three months in seclusion to finish her book.
examples.cn: 这位小说家闭门三个月，只为写完她的书。

examples.en: They chose a secluded beach for the wedding ceremony.
examples.cn: 他们选了一处僻静的海滩举行婚礼。

examples.en: After the scandal, he retreated into seclusion and stopped giving interviews.
examples.cn: 丑闻之后，他退隐了，不再接受采访。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞克路+神」——把路塞起来，人就躲进去了。这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 se-（分开）+ claudere（关闭）→ secludere（把……关在外面）→ seclusio（隔开）→ 英语 seclusion，核心义「关门隔离」。

sensesIntro.en: Seclusion moves from the abstract state of living apart, to a place that gives it, to freedom from disturbance, to the act of shutting off, and to the retreat itself.
sensesIntro.cn: seclusion 从「离群而居的状态」出发，依次引申为「提供这种状态的地方」「不受打扰」「隔离的动作」，最后指「隐居之所」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed door between you and the crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：你与人群之间的一扇关着的门。

branches.en: Living apart from others is the central human sense.
branches.cn: 离群而居是这个人本中心义项。

branches.en: A quiet place or retreat is the concrete side of the same state.
branches.cn: 僻静处与隐居之所是同一状态的具体一面。

branches.en: Freedom from disturbance is the positive reading of being closed off.
branches.cn: 不受打扰是被隔开之后的正面解读。

branches.en: The act sense keeps the verb seclude visible inside the noun.
branches.cn: 动作义项让动词 seclude 的影子留在名词里。

branches.en: All three travel back to the same Latin verb for shutting something off.
branches.cn: 这三者都回到同一个表示「关在外面」的拉丁动词。

intro.en: Seclusion is built on the Latin closing root claudere, with the verb seclude and the adjective secluded around it.
intro.cn: seclusion 建立在拉丁语「关闭」词根 claudere 之上，周围有动词 seclude 与形容词 secluded。

latinIntro.en: Latin se- means apart, and claudere means to close; together they give secludere, to shut off.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 se- 意为分开，claudere 意为关闭，合起来构成 secludere，意为关在外面。

items.example: The prefix se- marks separation.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 se- 标记分离。

items.example: Claudere gives the closing part of seclusion.
items.exampleCN: claudere 提供 seclusion 的「关闭」部分。

items.example: Secludere is the direct source verb.
items.exampleCN: secludere 是直接来源动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion turns a verb into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 把动词变成状态名词。

items.example: To seclude is to keep someone away from others.
items.exampleCN: seclude 指让人远离他人。

items.example: A secluded lane is quiet and private.
items.exampleCN: 僻静的小路安静而私密。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms seclusive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 seclusive。

items.example: Seclusive describes a person who likes being alone.
items.exampleCN: seclusive 形容喜欢独处的人。

items.meaning: the state of being shut off
items.example: Seclusion names the state itself.
items.exampleCN: seclusion 指这种状态本身。

definition_zh: 保密；守密（的状态）；秘密；隐蔽
definition_en: the quality or state of keeping something hidden from other people
core_image: 一只手把一个盒子按在怀里，盒盖紧合，不让旁人看见
scene: 谈判一直关起门来进行，内部消息不许外传。The talks were held in secrecy, and nothing said inside the room was reported.
sceneCN: 这里 secrecy 是「保密状态」（第 1 个义项：把某事藏在众人之外）；句意：谈判一直在保密状态下进行，屋里说过的话一句也没有对外透露。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，由名词收回形容词与名词用法，义为「秘密；秘密的」
形容词加后缀 -ly，义为「秘密地；暗中」
加后缀 -ive，义为「遮遮掩掩的；爱保密的」

senses.title: The state of being kept hidden
senses.definition: the condition of keeping information or activity away from public knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 把信息或活动置于公众知情之外的状态
senses.example: The plan was carried out in absolute secrecy.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划在绝对保密中进行。
senses.why: The Latin secretus means set apart or hidden, and secrecy names the state of staying hidden.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 secretus 意为「分开、藏起」，secrecy 指的就是「保持藏起来」这种状态。

senses.title: The practice of keeping secrets
senses.definition: the habit or policy of not telling others what one knows
senses.definitionCN: 不把知道的事告诉别人的习惯或政策
senses.example: The firm insists on secrecy about its client list.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司坚持对客户名单保密。
senses.why: A state can be turned into a rule people follow, so secrecy also names the practice itself.
senses.whyCN: 一种状态可以被变成人人遵守的规定，因此 secrecy 也指这种做法的本身。

senses.title: Protection from public view
senses.definition: the shelter of being away from public attention or observation
senses.definitionCN: 远离公众注意或观察的庇护
senses.example: The papers were handed over under cover of secrecy.
senses.exampleCN: 文件是在不为人知的情况下交出来的。
senses.why: Being hidden protects as well as conceals, so the word can suggest shelter from scrutiny.
senses.whyCN: 藏起来既掩盖，也提供保护，所以这个词也带「躲开审视」的意味。

senses.title: Official or institutional confidentiality
senses.definition: the legal duty of governments or organizations to keep certain information classified
senses.definitionCN: 政府或机构对特定信息予以保密的法定义务
senses.example: The law on official secrecy has been tightened.
senses.exampleCN: 官方保密法已经被收紧了。
senses.why: Once a state becomes a duty imposed by law, it turns into a policy of confidentiality.
senses.whyCN: 一旦状态成为法律强加的义务，它就变成了一套机密制度。

senses.title: Seclusion from human company
senses.definition: a being apart from other people, in quietness or privacy
senses.definitionCN: 远离他人，处于安静或私密之中
senses.example: He lived in secrecy in a small flat for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他多年来隐居在一间小公寓里。
senses.why: The same set-apart image can describe a person hidden from people rather than information hidden from view.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「隔开」的意象，既可以是信息藏起来，也可以是人躲开人群。

intro.en: Secrecy comes from Latin secretum, a secret, built on secretus, the past participle of secernere, to separate or set apart.
intro.cn: secrecy 来自拉丁语 secretum（秘密），其基础是 secretus，即 secernere（分开、筛出）的过去分词。

items.en: Secernere means to separate or set apart, made of se-, apart, and cernere, to sift.
items.cn: secernere 意为分开、筛出，由 se-（分开）与 cernere（筛选）构成。

items.en: Secretus, set apart, becomes the basis of secretum, a thing kept apart.
items.cn: secretus（被分开的）成为 secretum（被隔开的事物）的基础。

items.en: Secret enters Old French as both an adjective and a noun.
items.cn: secret 在古法语中同时作形容词和名词。

items.en: Secrecy is formed once secret is established, adding the suffix -cy to make a quality noun.
items.cn: secret 确立后，加上词尾 -cy 构成表性质的名词 secrecy。

items.en: The word settles into the fixed sense of the state of keeping things hidden.
items.cn: 现代英语中词义固定为「保守隐藏的状态」。

note.en: Secrecy is the noun of hiddenness, near secret, secretly, and secretive, and it shares a field with privacy, confidentiality, and concealment.
note.cn: secrecy 是表示「被藏起来」的名词，近邻是 secret、secretly、secretive，语义上属于私密、机密、掩盖这一群。

entries.definitionCN: 秘密地；暗中

normalIntro.en: Secrecy is the state built on secret, from Latin cernere, to sift out and set apart.
normalIntro.cn: secrecy 是建立在 secret 之上的状态名词，源自拉丁语 cernere（筛出、分开）。

normal.en: In secrecy describes doing something quietly and out of sight.
normal.cn: in secrecy 表示秘密地、暗中进行。

normal.en: A vow of secrecy is a promise not to reveal something.
normal.cn: a vow of secrecy 是承诺不泄露的誓言。

normal.en: The suffix -cy turns an adjective into a state noun, as in privacy.
normal.cn: 词尾 -cy 把形容词变成状态名词，privacy 同理。

normal.en: Swear someone to secrecy means to make them promise to keep quiet.
normal.cn: swear someone to secrecy 表示要求对方发誓守口如瓶。

normal.en: Compare honesty, which also names a personal quality, built with the same kind of suffix.
normal.cn: 对比 honesty，同样是带这类词尾的性格名词。

abstract.en: Picture a wax seal on an envelope, pressed shut so that no one can read inside.
abstract.cn: 想象信封上的一枚火漆印，压得严严实实，谁也不知道里面写了什么。

abstract.en: Imagine a doctor sworn to say nothing about a patient.
abstract.cn: 想象一位医生发誓不透露病人的任何情况。

abstract.en: Think of a curtain pulled across a window, hiding the room from the street.
abstract.cn: 想象把窗帘拉上，把房间从街面上遮住。

examples.en: Every member of the committee was sworn to secrecy.
examples.cn: 委员会的每一位成员都宣誓保密。

examples.en: The deal was signed in complete secrecy.
examples.cn: 这笔交易是在完全保密的情况下签署的。

examples.en: Some critics accuse the government of excessive secrecy.
examples.cn: 一些批评者指责政府保密过度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谁个说」——秘密一旦说出口，就不再是秘密，所以只能谁都不说。这是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 se-（分开）+ cernere（筛选）→ secernere（分开、筛出）→ secretus（被隔开的）→ secretum（秘密）→ 英语 secret + -cy → secrecy，核心义「隔开藏起」。

sensesIntro.en: Secrecy starts as the bare state of being hidden, extends to the practice of keeping secrets and the shelter it gives, then to institutional confidentiality and to a person hidden away.
sensesIntro.cn: secrecy 首先指「被藏起来」的状态，再扩展到守密的做法及其庇护作用，随后指制度层面的机密，最后指一个人躲开人群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed box held against the chest, its lid shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只紧贴怀中、盒盖紧闭的盒子。

branches.en: The plain state of being hidden is the core sense.
branches.cn: 单纯的隐藏状态是核心义项。

branches.en: Once the state becomes a habit, it turns into a practice.
branches.cn: 状态一旦成为习惯，就变成了做法。

branches.en: Hiding also shelters, so secrecy can mean cover from view.
branches.cn: 隐藏也提供庇护，所以 secrecy 可指躲开视线。

branches.en: Legal duty turns the practice into institutional confidentiality.
branches.cn: 法律责任把做法变成了制度性的机密。

branches.en: People as well as facts can be kept apart from the crowd.
branches.cn: 事实可以被隔开，人也可以被隔开于人群之外。

intro.en: Secrecy is the quality noun of secret, formed with -cy, and rests on the Latin sifting root cernere.
intro.cn: secrecy 是 secret 加词尾 -cy 构成的性质名词，根基是拉丁语表示「筛选」的 cernere。

latinIntro.en: Latin secernere means to separate, and secretus means set apart; the English -cy later makes the state noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secernere 意为分开，secretus 意为被隔开的；英语词尾 -cy 后来构成状态名词。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 se- 表示分离。

items.example: Cernere supplies the sifting image.
items.exampleCN: cernere 提供筛选的意象。

items.example: Secretus is the hidden one.
items.exampleCN: secretus 就是被藏起来的那个。

items.example: A secret is something kept from others.
items.exampleCN: secret 是不让他人知道的事。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾

items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cy 构成 privacy 这样的状态名词。

items.example: Secretly adds the adverb suffix -ly.
items.exampleCN: secretly 加了副词词尾 -ly。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms secretive.

items.example: Secretive describes a closed-off manner.
items.exampleCN: secretive 形容遮遮掩掩的做派。
